method: 14-agent audit/research workflow; every headline defect independently reproduced by a second agent

arch.summary: The solver is not a designer — it is a one-pass greedy pipeline (~1,620-line solve() over 8,905 lines) that places appliances per-wall in isolation, fills leftover gaps with largest-first width packing, derives uppers 1:1 from base seams, and then runs 30+ mutate-in-place "correction" passes to patch the result. There is no global objective, no room geometry model, no backtracking, and composition decisions (symmetry, rhythm, zone sequencing) are retrofitted as permutation passes that cannot change the widths chosen earlier — so they routinely fail (a plain 160"x130" L-shape yields 42"/16" range flanks, a 10" 3-drawer base, and a hood rendered 42" away from the range due to a cross-phase stale-position bug). Roughly 20 imported "expert" fixer modules (alignUppersToBase, enforceSymmetry, solveRoomExpert, insertWithCollisionCheck...) are imported but never called; Phase 8-10 subsystems only append warnings and never redesign anything. The 180/180 eval floor is self-referential: the aesthetic gate is the solver grading its own output (>=60), the design gate is just >=75% wall fill, and none of the concrete defects above fails any metric. "Right" (per the repo's own Cabinet-Placement guide and competitive research) means zone-planned, entry-aware, symmetric, standard-width compositions — which this architecture cannot reach by patching, because every patch runs after the decisions that matter are already frozen.

findings.title: Greedy per-wall solve with no global objective, no backtracking
findings.detail: solve() solves each wall independently (solveWall loop) after a fixed heuristic wall-assignment (longest wall = range+fridge, second = sink). The work triangle, aisle clearances, and cross-wall balance are only VALIDATED afterward — never optimized. When placement fails, 'rescue' passes re-pack appliances evenly instead of reconsidering earlier choices. A trivially ordinary input (L-shape 160"/130", 5 appliances) triggers the error path: range initially placed at 0 with a 'Wall A is too short' error on a 160-inch wall, then a work triangle of 368" (legs 135"/184" vs 108" max) that the solver merely warns about.
findings.evidence: solver.js:644-655 (per-wall loop), 480-517 (heuristic assignment), 2971-3305 (sequential per-appliance scoring, no joint search), 3307-3352 (rescue re-pack), live run output: 'Tight-Landing-Reduced-Clearance ... placed at 0' + 'work_triangle_large 368" > 312"' on walls 160/130

findings.title: Cross-phase state desync: hood placed 42 inches away from the range (reproduced)
findings.detail: centerCookingZone() (line 703) moves the range inside wallLayouts AFTER the appByWall position sync (lines 662-673), but solveUppers() reads range position from appByWall — so the hood skip-zone and hood cabinet use the PRE-centering position. Reproduced: range re-centered to 42-72, hood 'RH21 3624' emitted at position 0, and a gap-fill upper W3639 placed at 36-72 directly OVER the actual range. The comment at 697-700 claims the opposite ('Runs BEFORE the uppers solve so the hood follows the centered range'). This is the signature of the architecture: at least 4 mirrors of truth (wallLayouts cabinets, appByWall appliances, placements copies, _elev on sources) reconciled by ad-hoc sync loops keyed on wall|sku|position strings (1179-1189).
findings.evidence: solver.js:662-673 (sync), 703 (centering after sync), 3910-3915 + 4505-4520 (uppers read wallAppliances positions); reproduced output: range@42-72 but 'RH21 3624'@0 and gap-fill W3639@36 on the same wall; decisions log says 'Range re-centered at 57"'

findings.title: Width selection is largest-first greedy; composition is never an objective
findings.detail: fillSegment/greedyFill packs stock widths largest-first (42 then 36...), then patches the remainder with fillers or width-mods (regex SKU rewrite). This produces runs like B42-RT + B16-RTL flanking a range (42" vs 16") and a B3D10 (10-inch three-drawer base) — widths no designer would draw. Because widths freeze here, every later symmetry pass can only permute boxes, never resize them, so the 42/16 flank is unfixable downstream. The repo's own comments call an off-center range 'a classic auto-generated tell'.
findings.evidence: constraints.js:1627-1679 (greedyFill largest-first), solver.js:3487-3599 (fill + mod patching); live run: wall A = B42-RT | range | B16-RTL, wall B ends in B3D10

findings.title: Symmetry/centering passes can only reorder, not redesign — and silently no-op
findings.detail: centerCookingZone and centerSinkUnderWindow search prefix-splits of existing movable cabinets around anchors; they conserve widths and revert on any anomaly (both wrapped in try/catch non-fatal). In the reproduced run the best achievable prefix split left the range flanked 42/16 (centering 'succeeded' per the decision log while flanks stayed 2.6:1). applyRangeFlankSymmetry only fires when BOTH neighbors are plain bases. Symmetric width selection would have to happen during fill, where symmetry is only a boolean hint (preferSymmetric) on one zone type.
findings.evidence: solver.js:8130-8192 (centerCookingZone permutation-only), 8038-8122 (centerSinkUnderWindow), 2730-2780 (applyRangeFlankSymmetry guard), 702-709 (try/catch non-fatal); decisions log claims 'balanced flanking cabinets' over a 42/16 flank

findings.title: Auto-correction passes corrupt SKUs via first-digit regex replacement
findings.detail: Overlap/gap fixes rewrite widths with sku.replace(/\d+/, newWidth), which replaces the FIRST digit group. For drawer bases the first digits are the drawer count, not the width: 'B3D30' resized to 24 becomes 'B24D30'; 'B2TD24' -> 'B30TD24'; line 2637 strips the type via replace(/\d+/,'') turning 'B3D30' into 'BD30'. Verified with node. Five separate overlapping repair subsystems (solveWall chain steps 3-5 at 2543-2665, Project-5 correction loop at 998-1057, POST-PLACEMENT pass at 1196-1291, resolveOverflows at 1573, enforceFillerRule at 866) all fix the same overlap/gap failure mode — the definitional hotspot of repeated patching.
findings.evidence: solver.js:1015, 1027, 1046, 2637; node check: 'B3D30'.replace(/\d+/,'24') === 'B24D30'; five repair passes listed above; comment at 2858-2861 admits a past version 'shrank the sink base to width 0 (still fully priced)'

findings.title: Detect-but-never-redesign: the fixer modules are imported and never called
findings.detail: solver.js imports ~20 'expert' functions whose grep count is exactly 1 (the import line): alignUppersToBase, enforceSymmetry, solveFillers, solveRoomExpert, solveWorkTriangleExpert, insertWithCollisionCheck, resolveApplianceFirst, snapToNeighbor, snapToGrid, buildCabinetIntelligence, analyzeGaps, centerUpperRun, detectCommonLines, validateReveals, visibilityCheck, decomposeToStandardWidths, composeElevation, calculateElevationBalance, validatePlacement, linearValidateNKBA, solveIslandPlacement. Vertical seam alignment IS scored (scoreAlignment, warning when <50) but the aligner is never invoked; runProfessionalAudit grades A-F and nothing loops back. All Phase 8/9/10 subsystems only push validation entries — none changes a placement. 33 try/catch blocks degrade failures to info-level notes.
findings.evidence: grep counts: 21 imported functions with occurrence count 1 in solver.js (import-only); solver.js:1721-1731 (score + warn, no fix), 1757-1777 (audit merged as warnings only); imports at 22-213

findings.title: No room geometry model inside the solver
findings.detail: Corners are inferred from wall ARRAY ORDER (walls[0]/walls[1] assumed adjacent, all 90 degrees unless an explicit turn field), not from wall endpoints. The work-triangle coordinate builder maps every wall after index 0 onto the same y-axis at x = wallA.length — so triangle math is fiction for U/G shapes (wall 3 of a U gets wall-B coordinates). The Drawing-Quality-Audit confirms galley wall B draws outside the room because both walls share one frame; per CLAUDE.md the actual world-frame logic lives in FloorPlanView, not the engine. Islands are placed by the renderer with defaults (audit A5).
findings.evidence: solver.js:2022-2034 (corner pairs by index), 8319-8331 (2D coords wrong for >2 walls), docs/Drawing-Quality-Audit.md A1/A5, CLAUDE.md ('FloorPlanView ... per-wall world-frame logic that the 3D view reuses')

findings.title: Zone 'model' is a post-hoc label, not a plan
findings.detail: classifyZone() names a segment after whichever appliance happens to border it AFTER placement (rangeFlanking/sinkAdjacent/fridgeAdjacent/general). The repo's own Cabinet-Placement-and-Appliance-Guide specifies the actual standard: five task zones sequenced from the entry (consumables nearest entry, prep between cleaning and cooking, non-consumables beside the DW). The solver has no entry/door awareness in wall assignment — 'fridge near entry' is hardcoded as 'left end by convention' (2936-2938) regardless of where doors actually are; doors only function as keep-out rectangles.
findings.evidence: solver.js:3607-3629 (classifyZone), 2909-2938 (fridge terminal convention), docs/Cabinet-Placement-and-Appliance-Guide.md sections 1.1/1.3 (zone sequence the solver never computes)

findings.title: Uppers are cloned from base seams, never composed
findings.detail: solveUppers emits exactly one upper per base cabinet with width = findClosestWidth(base.width, 'down'), copying base seams upward and shedding slivers (a 16" base gets a 15" upper + 1" hole); closeUpperGaps then patches the holes with gap-fill cabinets. There is no independent upper composition (equal-width pairs flanking the hood, balanced runs) — which is why the wall-A uppers in the reproduction are W15 + RW36 + hood + a 36" gap-filler. The imported centerUpperRun/alignUppersToBase that could compose runs are never called.
findings.evidence: solver.js:4215-4453 (per-base loop, findClosestWidth 'down', alignedWithBase), 3828-3866 (closeUpperGaps patching), reproduction output UPPERS A: W1539L@72 + W3639@36 'gap-fill' overlapping the range

findings.title: The 180/180 eval floor is self-referential and cannot see any of the above
findings.detail: scoreKitchen passes a kitchen on: cabinets exist + wall-fill >=75%, SKUs price, no spatial-validator errors, NKBA report >=70, and aesthetic >=60 — where 'aesthetic' is the solver's OWN scoreAesthetics grading its own output (the reproduced kitchen scores 66 with symmetry 57 and STILL passes). Hood-not-over-range, 42/16 flanks, 10" drawer bases, corrupted SKUs that still resolve, and 'Tight-Landing' errors (rule name doesn't match the /NKBA/i filter) all pass. scoreAgainstTraining is an 8-boolean fingerprint match (gola/island/two-tone/stacked/...) used as metadata; it never steers a decision. The three-option feature just re-runs the same solver with pref presets, so all options share every structural defect.
findings.evidence: evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs:61 (fill>=0.75), 116-124 (/NKBA/i filter misses Tight-Landing errors), 127-136 (self-graded aesthetic >=60); solver.js:8521-8672 (fingerprint matcher); eclipse-engine/src/designOptions.js:74-86 (options = prefs presets over same solve)

findings.title: Dead/broken subsystems shipped inside solve()
findings.detail: (a) Crown/light-rail extrusion never runs: moldingPaths is an object {crown, lightRail} but the gate tests moldingPaths?.length (undefined) — moldingExtrusion/lightRailExtrusion are always null and metadata.crownMoldingLinearFt is always 0. (b) Door-swing collision warnings emit 'undefined vs undefined' / '[object Object] vs [object Object]' (8 per ordinary solve). (c) constraint-propagation warns 'Last cabinet position_end 124 !== wallEnd 160' on every corner wall because runs don't understand corner consumption. Each is a subsystem that LOOKS like capability in the return payload but contributes noise or nothing.
findings.evidence: solver.js:1127-1130 (object) vs 1685,1691 (?.length gate), reproduction output: 8x 'door_swing_collision ... undefined vs undefined', 2x constraint_propagation false positives on a clean L-shape

findings.title: History confirms the hotspot: every recorded fix is a patch to the patching machinery
findings.detail: Only 7 commits touch solver.js (phase-squashed history), but the in-file archaeology is the real log of repeated same-area fixes: temporal-dead-zone crash in the filler validation pass (871-874); duplicate over-fridge RW emitted by two competing paths, double-billed on real quotes (890-906, Drawing-Quality-Audit P0); sink base shrunk to width 0 while still priced (2858-2861); mounting rails silently skipped for EVERY kitchen due to an id/wallId mismatch and the si scorer crediting lazy susans as zero (CLAUDE.md Phase 0, commit b084719); commit c3ec705 revealed corners were being skipped entirely for short-code layouts so the eval only 'looked green'. The recurring themes — overlap repair, duplicate emission, stale copies, silently-skipped subsystems — are all consequences of the mutate-in-place multi-copy pipeline, not independent bugs.
findings.evidence: git log --oneline solver.js (7 commits: 86a489b, b084719, c3ec705, 5b4d335, 9de5ff0, 2f92971, 16621bc); solver.js:871-874, 890-906, 2858-2861; CLAUDE.md 'Phase 0 fixes' paragraph; docs/Drawing-Quality-Audit.md 'Fixed during the audit'

findings.title: What 'right' means is already written down in-repo — the architecture just can't express it
findings.detail: The Cabinet-Placement guide (per-layout placement rules: 'fridge at one leg-end, range at the other, sink in the middle under a window', 9-12" pull-outs flanking the range, tall units grouped at leg-ends) and the competitive research ('center verb', Winner's manufacturer intelligence, ProKitchen Fit) define the target: standard-width, zone-sequenced, symmetric compositions with contextual centering. Each of these is a WHOLE-WALL composition constraint; the current engine makes width, position, and type decisions in separate irreversible phases, so no amount of additional passes can jointly satisfy them. That is the structural cap on quality.
findings.evidence: docs/Cabinet-Placement-and-Appliance-Guide.md 1.2-1.3, docs/Design-Studio-Competitive-Research.md sections 1-2; contrast with solver.js phase ordering (positionAppliances -> fillWallSegment -> center* -> repair passes)

recommendations: Replace the phase pipeline's core with generate-and-score: for each wall (and the room jointly), enumerate a handful of CANDIDATE compositions (appliance positions x standard-width fill patterns, symmetric variants included) and score them with one global objective (zone sequence, triangle, symmetry, standard-width usage, filler count) — keep the existing passes only as scorers, not mutators. The existing per-position scoring loops show the scoring vocabulary already exists; it is just applied one decision at a time.

Introduce a single source of truth for placement state (one run model per wall with derived views) and make every pass operate on it; delete the appByWall/wallLayouts/placements/_elev mirror-sync loops. The reproduced hood-off-range bug is a direct consequence of the mirrors and will keep recurring in new forms until this lands.

Choose widths for symmetry at fill time: when a range/hood or window is in a segment, solve the two flanks as one constrained pair (equal standard widths) instead of greedy largest-first + post-hoc permutation. This single change eliminates the most visible 'auto-generated tell' (42/16 flanks, 10-inch drawer bases).

Fix the two live bugs found: (a) SKU width rewrites must use a family-aware builder (buildSku) instead of sku.replace(/\d+/,...) — currently corrupts B3D/B2TD/B4D family SKUs; (b) the moldingPaths?.length gate (solver.js:1685,1691) tests an object for array length, permanently disabling crown/light-rail extrusion.

Give the solver real geometry: compute wall endpoints/normals once (promote FloorPlanView's world-frame math into the engine), derive corners from geometry not array order, and fix buildValidationInput's 2D coordinates for 3+ wall layouts so triangle math stops being fiction for U/G shapes.

Break the self-grading eval loop: score the si corpus against EXTERNAL references — the 47 training projects and real acknowledgment kitchens (Mautz, Soderstrom) as golden layouts, plus targeted assertions that would have caught today's findings (hood centered over range within 1", no cabinet narrower than 12" outside filler roles, flank ratio <= 1.5 at focal points, no non-catalog SKU strings in placements, zero 'undefined' text in validation messages).

Either call or delete the ~20 imported-but-unused expert modules; every one that stays should be wired as a scorer or a candidate generator. An 8,900-line file where a third of the imports are dead is itself a defect that hides which machinery actually runs.

output.summary: Programmatic sweep of solve() over all 36 templates + 60-kitchen si corpus (96 runs, 1,041 cabinets; script at /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/sweep.mjs, raw JSON at sweep-results.json). The owner is right: the 180/180 floor is cosmetic. The solver ships kitchens its OWN validator marks severity=error (range touching fridge, range-in-corner, wall overflow) because evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs scoreNkba() only fails on errors whose rule name matches /NKBA/, and solver.js demotes every NKBA landing/triangle rule to advisory warnings. Measured against NKBA numbers: 37/96 kitchens violate landing minimums, 75/79 have a work-triangle leg outside 4-9 ft, ranges are placed hard against refrigerators in 6 corpus kitchens, 73/96 kitchens contain at least one 9-12 inch sliver cabinet (65/96 get a 9-inch W9xx upper jammed beside the hood), 31/96 have a wall with exactly one cabinet, and 45/96 leave >12 inches of bare wall above base runs. Three interior design passes (part IDs, style morph, vertical alignment) crash on 96/96 runs and are swallowed as warnings, and the door-swing detector emits ~9 garbage "undefined vs undefined" warnings per kitchen. The dominant failure mode is a left-packed streaming packer: appliances anchored at position 0 (fridge@0 | range@36), remaining width streamed into cabinets, leaving zero landings, 36-inch median flanking asymmetry, and sliver leftovers — the opposite of how a designer composes around centered appliances.

findings.title: Solver ships layouts its own validator marks severity=error; eval cannot see them
findings.detail: 8/96 kitchens carry severity=error validation entries and still 'pass' everything: Cyncly-Range-Fridge-Buffer ('Range and fridge are 0" apart — minimum 9" buffer required') on si:K003/K004/K024/K027/K044/K051; Cyncly-Range-In-Corner on tpl:u_shape_compact; wall_overflow x2 on tpl:single_wall_entertainer. evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs scoreNkba() (line ~116-123) only fails on errors matching /NKBA/i, so Cyncly-* and wall_overflow errors pass the NKBA metric; scoreFloorplan only reads spatialValidation.errors, not result.validation. This is why 180/180 coexists with layouts the engine itself calls errors.

findings.title: Range placed hard against refrigerator (0-inch gap) — signature layout of small L/U kitchens
findings.detail: The appliance placer anchors fridge at wall position 0 and streams the range immediately after it: 'refrigerator@0 w36 | range@36 w36'. Result: fridge has 0" landing on both sides, range has 0" landing on one side, and the range-fridge triangle leg is 36" (NKBA minimum 48"). This exact pattern appears in 6 of 60 corpus kitchens and is the single worst repeated output.
findings.evidence: si:K004 base wall A(120"): refrigerator@0w36 | range@36w36 | BEP3/4@71.3 | B12-RTL@72w12; solver's own messages: 'NKBA-Landing-Fridge: Fridge handle-side landing 0" < 15"', 'NKBA-Triangle-Leg-Short: Range-to-fridge 36" < 48"', 'Cyncly-Range-Fridge-Buffer: 0" apart' — all shipped as warnings/uncaught error

findings.title: Three design passes crash on EVERY kitchen and are swallowed as warnings
findings.detail: part_id_error: 'Part ID generation: Invalid room type: kitchen' (the part-ID generator rejects the most common room type) — 96/96 runs; style_morph_error: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'forEach')" — 96/96; alignment_error: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')" — 96/96, so metadata.verticalAlignmentScore is null in every kitchen (verified 12/12 sample). These features (part IDs, style morphing, vertical seam alignment scoring) are effectively dead in production and nothing fails.
findings.evidence: sweep validationHist: WARN part_id_error:96, WARN style_morph_error:96, WARN alignment_error:96 out of 96 runs; direct probe: nullAlign=12/12; messages captured from si:K004 validation array

findings.title: Door-swing detector emits garbage: 859 warnings, mostly 'undefined vs undefined'
findings.detail: 859 door_swing_collision warnings across 96 runs (~9/kitchen). Sampled 12 kitchens: 101 of 117 messages read 'Door swing collision: undefined vs undefined' — the detector loses cabinet identities, so real collisions are indistinguishable from noise and every downstream consumer (order desk, QA) learns to ignore the rule.
findings.evidence: validationHist 'WARN door_swing_collision': 859; 12-kitchen sample: swingTot=117, swingUndefinedMsg=101

findings.title: NKBA landings failed in 37/96 kitchens (52 violations) — even after crediting dishwasher counter as landing
findings.detail: Measured contiguous counter beside each appliance (counting DW/wine/bev counter and corner spans as landing): sink violations in 30 kitchens (sink at a wall end with 0" on one side, e.g. K003 sink B L60/R0 vs required 18/24), range/cooktop 12 (L0 beside fridge), fridge 10 (max landing 0" < 15"). The solver flags many of these itself (123x NKBA-Landing-Sink, 42x Landing-Range, 26x Landing-Fridge warnings) then ships anyway.

findings.title: Work triangle out of NKBA range in 75 of 79 measurable kitchens
findings.detail: Of 79 runs with all three appliances placed, 75 have at least one leg outside 4-9 ft and 39 have total run outside 13-26 ft (u_island_entertainer: sink-range 15.8 ft, sink-fridge 15.1 ft, total 37.7 ft; K004: range-fridge 3.0 ft). 17 runs have no measurable triangle. Corroborated by the solver's own warnings: NKBA-Triangle-Leg-Long x71, work_triangle_leg_long x69, leg-short x33 — all advisory.

findings.title: Sliver cabinets everywhere: 11.2% of all cabinets are <=12 inches; 65/96 kitchens get a 9-inch upper
findings.detail: 117 of 1,041 cabinets are 9-12" wide (47 exactly 12", 70 in 9-12"); 73/96 kitchens have at least one. The packer's leftover-width tell: W939R x42 and W948R x20 (9" single-door uppers wedged at wall start beside the hood run), B12-RTL x14, B3D12/W1239 x23. Real kitchens favor 15-36" units; a 9" upper at the end of a run is what a human designer absorbs by widening neighbors.

findings.title: No symmetric flanking: median counter asymmetry around range is 36 inches; around sink 36 inches
findings.detail: Counter run left vs right of the cooking appliance differs by >18" in 55/83 instances (median 36", e.g. range L0/R48); sink >18" in 66/95 (median 36", u_island_entertainer sink L0/R132 — 11 feet of counter on one side, zero on the other). The solver's own hood_flanking_asymmetry fired 71x (e.g. '9" left vs 0.75" right'). Layouts read as left-packed streams, not composed elevations.

findings.detail: After excusing hood, fridge cabinet, sink window zone, and corner consumption, upper runs still leave gaps over normal base cabinets: mean 16.4"/kitchen; tpl:open_concept_l 75", tpl:island_centerpiece 57", tpl:l_shape_standard and tpl:peninsula_l_shape 48", si:K032 46.5" (bare wall from 37.5-57" between the 9" upper and the hood). findings.detail: Typical: si:K004 wall B (96") base run = one B3D24 flanked by floating 0.75" end panels; its upper run = one W2439L. si:K032 wall B (120") = one B3D48. These walls look unfinished in the floor plan and waste the U-shape's prime storage wall.

findings.detail: BEP3/4-FTK end panels are inserted mid-run, e.g. K004 wall A: BEP@71.25 sandwiched between the range and B12-RTL, and FWEP wall-end panels float at x=35.25 next to nothing. findings.detail: 60 corpus kitchens dedupe to 42 distinct solved layouts (ceiling-only variants K004=K024=K044 produce byte-identical plans), so 180/180 overstates coverage ~30%. Output monotony: SKU families across all 96 runs are W:488, B:248, SB:95, RH:83, BWDMA:82 — the same BWDMA waste cabinet in ~85% of kitchens, only 3 glass-door units, 2 blind-corner bases in wall runs, drawer:door base ratio 100:149 (40% drawers, low for contemporary work).

findings.title: What 'right' means, in numbers the current stack never checks
findings.detail: A defensible definition from this sweep: (1) zero severity=error of ANY rule name; (2) NKBA landings met (15" fridge, 12/15 range, 18/24 sink) — currently failed by 37/96; (3) all triangle legs 4-9 ft — currently failed by 75/79; (4) no cabinet under 12" unless user-forced — currently 117 slivers; (5) range/sink flanking asymmetry <= 12" — current median 36"; (6) upper coverage gap <= 12"/wall — currently failed by 45/96; (7) no internal pass crashes — currently 3 passes crash on 96/96. Each is already computable from solve() output; none is enforced by scoreKitchen.mjs today.
findings.evidence: All numbers from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-End-to-End/a0b36111-8056-5289-9cca-10d3b5c7db60/scratchpad/sweep-results.json (agg block), reproducible via sweep.mjs in the same directory

recommendations: Make ANY severity=error fail the si eval: in evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs scoreNkba/scoreFloorplan, drop the /NKBA/i rule-name filter and count Cyncly-*, wall_overflow, and range-in-corner errors as hard fails; stop demoting NKBA-Landing-*/Triangle to advisory in solver.js (ADVISORY_RULES around line 1878) for the eval path.

Fix appliance placement before cabinet packing: enforce a minimum 15-24 inch counter buffer between range/cooktop and refrigerator, never anchor the fridge at position 0 without an enclosure/panel run, and pull the sink off open wall ends (K003/K004/K024/K027/K044/K051 are ready-made regression fixtures — their exact base listings are in sweep-results.json).

Add a leftover-width redistribution pass: when the packer's remainder is under 15 inches, widen neighboring cabinets (3-inch increments or width-mods) instead of emitting W939/W948/B12 slivers; gate with a new eval metric 'no cabinet 1-12 inches wide' (currently 117 offenders).

Add a flanking-symmetry objective around range/hood and sink (target |L-R| <= 12 inches; current median 36) and an upper-continuity pass that extends upper runs over bare base cabinets (45/96 kitchens have >12 inches of bare wall).

Repair the three universally-crashing passes: part-id-generator rejects roomType 'kitchen'; style-morphing and vertical-alignment both dereference undefined; fix the door-swing warning payload ('undefined vs undefined' in 101/117 sampled) — then make internal pass exceptions fail tests instead of appending warnings.

Fix positional defects: wall_overflow packing in single_wall_entertainer (242.25 on a 240 wall, fridge offset 2.25), undefined tall positions in u_shape_gourmet/u_island_entertainer/bar_wet_bar/butler_pantry, and end panels inserted mid-run (81 warnings).

Stop emitting SKUs whose printed size disagrees with geometry (115 mismatches like B2HD22.23L at 23.25, SB30 at 23.25): either rename to the true modified width using the catalog width-mod convention or emit standard width + filler.

Diversify the corpus (60 kitchens collapse to 42 distinct layouts; vary appliance walls/positions, not just ceiling) and add the worst-5 kitchens from this sweep as named golden fixtures with the stricter thresholds above, so the floor measures design quality rather than crash-freedom.

visual.summary: I SSR-rendered 10 auto-solved kitchens (8 templates + 2 evals/si corpus kitchens) to PNGs via the esbuild+resvg pipeline and reviewed 20+ floor plans and range-wall elevations by eye. The owner is right: the solver's output is not a designed kitchen, it is appliance placement plus filler. The recurring visual signature is a range wall with a floating hood and almost no upper cabinets (often literally zero, or one 9-15 inch sliver), ranges flanked by identical plain door cabinets with zero drawer bases anywhere in the kitchen, appliances shaved to fractional widths (a 29.25 inch refrigerator), sink/range/fridge packed with zero landing counter between them, and invented non-catalog SKUs (BWDMA42 trash pull-out, B35-RT, W5448) as the largest cabinets on a wall. Floor plans additionally have severe annotation collisions (tag circles printed over cabinet labels, dims through text). The 180/180 si eval floor sees none of this because the scorer never measures upper-run composition, symmetry, catalog membership, or landing zones. Every finding below names the kitchen/wall and comes from the rendered image; renders are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-End-to-End/a0b36111-8056-5289-9cca-10d3b5c7db60/scratchpad/renders/.

findings.title: Range walls have no designed upper composition — hood floats on bare wall
findings.detail: The focal wall of nearly every kitchen renders as a hood suspended over empty wall. l_shape_standard Wall B: ZERO upper cabinets on the whole 120 inch range wall — 60 inches of blank wall above the counter on both sides of the hood. galley_large Wall B: one W3627 stranded mid-wall left of the hood with a gap to the hood, nothing at all right of the hood (39+ inches bare). galley_small Wall B: nothing right of the hood; the only uppers are the over-fridge cabinet and a lone 15 inch W1527R. u_shape_family Wall C: one 24 inch W2424L jammed between hood and fridge (its outline overlaps the hood skirt), zero uppers over the 54+ inches of base run left of the hood. corpus_K018 Wall A: nothing right of the hood. A designer composes symmetric uppers flanking the hood to the corners; the solver's upper packer clearly dies or gives up on walls containing hood+refrigerator.

findings.title: Zero drawer bases; ranges flanked by identical plain-door cabinets

Ranges are always flanked by matched pairs of door-front roll-out cabinets (B27-RT, B35-RT, B39-RT, B42-RT — schedule notes '2 dr'), which render as blank double doors, so the range wall reads as monotone slabs. single_wall_entertainer is the extreme: a 20 foot wall of REF + four identical B42-RT + range. solver.js lines 3690-3694 claim 'Frameless default: B3D drawer base... in all zones', but the rendered output shows the range-flank branch (line 3658, B-RT) wins everywhere and the B3D preference never materializes on perimeter walls. A kitchen with no drawer stack near the range fails basic NKBA storage planning and looks like builder-grade filler.

findings.title: Eval blindness: why 180/180 coexists with all of the above
findings.detail: Each defect above appears in kitchens that pass evals/si/run-corpus.mjs 180/180. The 5-metric scorer (scoreKitchen.mjs) evidently checks base-run fill, price, NKBA subset, but never: upper-run coverage/symmetry on the range wall, seam alignment, appliance-width integrity, landing clearances between specific appliance pairs, emitted-SKU catalog membership, or annotation legibility. The owner's 'never been right' is precisely the space the scorer does not measure — the eval floor is a packing check, not a design check.
findings.evidence: corpus_K004 (range against fridge, one 9-inch upper) and corpus_K018 (35.25-inch fridge, 9-inch upper) are passing corpus members; contrast with their renders listed above

recommendations: Build a range-wall upper composer: symmetric upper runs flanking the hood, filling from hood to corners, seams snapped to base seams, centered on the range centerline; treat hood+fridge walls as the primary composition, not the leftover. Verify by re-rendering l_shape_standard Wall B and galley_large Wall B.

Enforce per-family width domains when minting SKUs (solver.js sizedSku/width-append path, ~line 3707): clamp/split to catalog-legal widths and add a hard eval that every emitted SKU resolves in the active tenant catalog — that alone kills BWDMA30/36/42, B35-RT, W5448, W1112.

Never resize appliances or sink cabinets to absorb remainders — appliances are fixed-width; absorb slack in fillers or by resizing flexible cabinets. Add scorer check: appliance rendered width == input width, and schedule width == plan geometry width.
Add adjacency/landing rules to the packer and the scorer: min 15-18 inch counter landing beside range and fridge, prep run between sink and range (fixes corpus_K004 and single_wall_compact).

Honor the existing B3D preference on perimeter walls: at least one drawer stack adjacent to the range and one near the sink; cap consecutive identical door cabinets at two (fixes the four-B42-RT wall).

Set a minimum useful cabinet width (~12 inch base, ~12-15 inch upper) and merge slivers into neighbors; forbid a sliver from being the only upper on a wall; fix the 12-inch-high-upper selection so upper heights fill the datum-to-54AFF band (u_shape_gourmet).

Fix the rendered-overlap and zero-width-part emissions (single_wall_entertainer OVERLAP 3, W=0 end panels) — these are solver placement bugs visible in output, and the existing tools/audit-drawings.jsx text-collision/overlap linter should be promoted into evals/_cross so annotation collisions and overlap flags fail CI.

Extend evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs with visual-composition metrics computed from solver geometry: upper-coverage ratio over base run per wall, seam-alignment score, hood-flank symmetry, corner-termination, so the 180/180 floor starts measuring what a designer sees.

realdiff.summary: I reconstructed the Mautz kitchen (the same real, professionally-designed U-shape the pricing suite locks to the penny: walls 125.125/102.75/112.5, sink+DW on A, 30" range on B, 36" fridge on C, 96" ceiling) from evals/_cross/fixtures/mautz-drawings-pages.json and ran solve() on that exact room. Head-to-head, auto-solve reproduces only 4 of the human designer's 16 identifiable design decisions outright (4 more partially, 8 not at all — ~25% strict, ~38% with half-credit). The auto layout also fails on its own terms: the solver's own validator raises 3 errors (range-in-corner x2, tight landing) yet metadata still reports nkbaScore=100 and scoreAgainstTraining gives it 100/100 confidence — direct proof the 180/180 eval floor measures nothing about design quality. Beyond decision misses, I found four hard defects: every upper corner gets a duplicated WSC24-PH ($1,010 charged twice per corner, against the code's own "one per corner" comment); walls[] and placements[] disagree about what cabinet sits at the same position (BWDMA29 vs B3D29 — elevation and quote show different cabinets); an explicitly requested wallOven is silently dropped with zero warning in 2 of 3 training-profile rooms; and auto-emitted pseudo-SKUs mis-price through the normalizer (LR-SQ-8' becomes a $2,463 island end cap, a range hood prices at $30, DW panels become $0.71 profile fillers). Qualitative comparison against soderstrom_kitchen, josh_huang, and mccomb TRAINING_PROFILES notes shows the same pattern: auto reproduces the generic skeleton (sink base, hood, fridge panels, an occasional tower) but never the features that define each real project — tall appliance walls, twin super susans, oven/micro combos, wine/waste specialty bases, glass bar uppers, apron sinks.

findings.title: Auto-solve reproduces ~4/16 of the real designer's decisions on the golden Mautz room
findings.detail: Decision-by-decision diff on the identical room. MATCHED (4): lazy-susan at range/fridge corner (BL36-PHR vs BL36-SS-PH), DW adjacent to sink, 93" fridge end panels (FREP3/4 93FTK vs REP1.5 93FTK-27), RW over-fridge cabinet (RW3624 vs RW3621-27). PARTIAL (4): sink base (SB36 vs SB36-FHD variant), waste base near sink (18" BWDMW18 vs 29" auto unit), drawer bank (human's B24-2D + B3D15 pair vs one non-catalog B3D41), over-range treatment (W3624 24"-high cab vs RH21 3624 hood). MISSED (8): BBC45R blind corner at sink/range corner (auto uses a second $2,046 super susan — $708 BBC45 is what the human chose); the 93" tall pantry U22 1/2-93R ($1,455) — auto emits ZERO tall storage cabinets for this kitchen; fridge mid-wall with pantry beyond it (auto shoves fridge to the wall end); open window zone over the sink with an IWS30 shelf (auto slams a W3639 upper directly over the sink); no upper corner cabinets — human closes both upper corners with F339 fillers, auto installs four WSC24-PH; the WSE2430-39R decorative open end shelf ($2,006) terminating the upper run; widths tuned to the wall (W28.539, W4239, W1239R) with fillers closing every run to the inch; and a 6.75" range landing filler package (F634 1/2 + BEP3/4L-FTK). Line-item volume: human 21 items, auto 41 "cabinets" + 19 accessories = 60.
findings.evidence: parseDesignPdf(mautz-drawings-pages.json) → 21 wallItems across walls A/B/C (elevation pages 2-4 titled SINK/RANGE/FRIDGE give per-wall order); solve() output run in scratchpad/mautz-diff.mjs: TALLS array empty, uppers include W3639 at x=24-60 over the sink at x=24.13-60.13, placements contain 4x WSC24-PH and metadata.totalCabinets=41

findings.title: Duplicated upper corner cabinet: two WSC24-PH pushed per corner despite 'one per corner' comment
findings.detail: solveUpperCorners pushes WSC24-PH twice (side:left then side:right) for every corner, directly under the comment 'Catalog format: WSC24-PH (single SKU, no height suffix, no L/R — one per corner)'. Mautz auto output carries 4 upper corner susans for 2 corners (metadata.totalUpperCorners=4). At $1,010 each that is $2,020 of phantom cost per U-shape kitchen plus physically overlapping geometry in the corner. The human design uses zero upper corner cabinets.

findings.title: Explicitly requested wall oven silently dropped from the layout, no warning emitted
findings.detail: For the mccomb- and josh_huang-modeled rooms (u-shape, wallOven pinned to a named wall), the solved output contains no oven tower and no error/warning: talls = [UT2496 pantry_tower (never requested), fridge panels]. solveTalls (solver.js:4845-4895) does build an oven tower, so the drop happens downstream (tall consolidation/placement, ~solver.js:5250-5262). The customer asked for a wall oven; the design just doesn't have one, and validation is silent about it. In the soderstrom l-shape room the oven tower survived (FIO3093-27.875), so this is layout-dependent, which makes it worse — it passes casual spot checks.

findings.title: walls[] and placements[] disagree about which cabinet occupies the same position
findings.detail: In the Mautz auto output, wall A's cabinets array contains BWDMA29 (waste pull-out) at position 60.13, while placements[] lists B3D29 (3-drawer base) at the same x=60.13 with the same role 'sinkAdjacent'. compilePlacements runs at solver.js:908, then Phase 6d (solver.js:930-960) and the G15 NKBA waste pass (solver.js:8196-8225) mutate cabinet SKUs afterward — one view gets the mutation, the other doesn't. Consequence: the elevation (renders from walls/uppers) and the quote (prices from placements) show the customer two different cabinets. Note also the two passes encode contradictory rules, and the real Mautz designer contradicts the Diehl rule the code cites: Mautz has DW on the sink wall AND a BWDMW18 waste base.
findings.evidence: mautz-diff.mjs output: 'WALL(base) A ... BWDMA29 w=29 pos=60.13 sinkAdjacent' vs 'PLACEMENTS ... A B3D29 w=29 x=60.13 base sinkAdjacent'; solver.js:908 (compilePlacements) precedes the SKU-mutating passes at 930-960 and 8196-8225

findings.title: Auto layout fails the solver's own validator (3 errors) while nkbaScore reports 100 and training confidence reports 100
findings.detail: On the Mautz room, solve() returns validation containing errors 'Cyncly-Range-In-Corner' (twice) and 'Tight-Landing-Reduced-Clearance' plus 13 warnings (0" sink landing, 0.75" range landing, work-triangle legs 137-146" over the 108" max, three constraint_propagation run-closure mismatches), yet metadata.nkbaScore=100 and scoreAgainstTraining() returns confidence 100, closestMatch 'Gable'. The root design cause: the solver spends two 36" super susans (72") of the 102.75" range wall, leaving exactly 30.75" and then errors on its own range placement — while the human freed that wall by choosing a BBC45R blind at the A/B corner. The eval floor (180/180) inherits these saturated metrics: scoreAgainstTraining compares only 8 booleans (layout/gola/island/twoTone/B2TD/DP/stacked/cab-count-range, solver.js:8594-8633), so a layout with a range jammed in a corner and no pantry scores identically to the real Gable project.
findings.evidence: mautz-diff2.mjs: validation array with 3 error-severity entries and nkbaScore:100 in metadata; scoreAgainstTraining → {confidence:100, closestMatch:'Gable'}; scoring weights at solver.js:8598-8629

findings.title: Runs don't close to the wall: 14" upper hole, 0.5" overrun, panel placed past the wall end
findings.detail: Mautz auto wall A uppers: W2439R(0-24), W3639(24-60), W2739(60-87), then nothing until the corner unit at ~101.1 — a 14.1" open gap mid-run with no cabinet and no filler (metadata.totalFillers=1 for the whole kitchen; the human used four fillers, F634 1/2/F339x2/F393, to close every run to the inch). Wall C: fridge spans 77-113 on a 112.5" wall (0.5" overrun) and the left fridge panel REP1.5 93FTK-27L is placed at x=113.0, entirely beyond the wall. The solver's own constraint_propagation warnings confirm: 'Last cabinet position_end 89.75 !== wallEnd 125.125' (and 30.75 vs 102.75, 77.75 vs 112.5). A dealer cannot install this drawing.

findings.title: Auto-emitted SKUs are not catalog codes and mis-price through the normalizer, both directions
findings.detail: The solver fabricates width-interpolated and pseudo SKUs that findSku() cannot resolve literally: B3D41, B3D29, B41-RT, B3D42, B3D37, B33-RT (real designers pick catalog widths — Mautz uses B24-2D + B3D15 — and close gaps with fillers), plus internal tokens like EDGTL|34.5|44|0.75 (island end, no price at all). The normalized fallback then produces silent garbage: LR-SQ-8' light-rail resolves to ISL-ELR24 (island end cap) at $2,463 — a phantom ~$2.4k on every auto kitchen that emits the standard moulding kit; 'RH21 3624' range hood resolves to accessory RH21 at $30; DWP-24/DW-TK-24/FDP-36/GRILLE-36 appliance panels (emitted unconditionally even though Mautz has no panel-ready appliances) resolve to 'PROFILE FILLER' at $0.711 each. The auto bill of materials is neither order-grade nor honestly priced.
