findings.title: What 'right' means, operationalized: the human design is a set of checkable invariants the evals never assert
findings.detail: From the Mautz + Wilterding fixtures and the profile notes, 'right' decomposes into testable rules auto currently fails: (a) every run closes to the printed wall dim with fillers >=3" (human: 4 fillers, zero gaps; auto: 1 filler, 14" gap, 0.5" overrun); (b) tall storage exists and anchors the fridge (pantry adjacent, fridge mid-wall); (c) sink wall respects the window (no upper over sink); (d) corner treatment is chosen per wall budget (blind on the tight corner frees the range wall — the exact failure that made auto's own validator error); (e) widths come from the catalog page, not interpolation; (f) specialty storage (waste, wine, tray, rollout) appears at the frequencies the training corpus documents; (g) nothing the customer specified disappears. None of these are asserted anywhere in evals/si (the 5-metric scorer) or evals/run.mjs — which is exactly why 180/180 coexists with 'never been right'.
findings.evidence: Human fixture: parseDesignPdf report.edges all match:true against printed dims 102.75/112.5/125.125; auto constraint_propagation warnings on all 3 walls; evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs metrics and scoreAgainstTraining booleans (solver.js:8598-8629) contain no per-decision assertions

recommendations: Turn the two real drawing sets into a design-diff eval: parse mautz/wilterding fixtures with parseDesignPdf, auto-solve the same reconstructed room, and assert per-decision reproduction (corner types, tall presence, no-upper-over-sink, run closure to printed dim, catalog-width-only SKUs, appliance count in == appliance count out). Gate the phase plan on decision-reproduction %, not on the current boolean/si floors.

Fix the four hard defects first, in this order: (1) remove the duplicated WSC24-PH push (solver.js:4775-4796); (2) make Phase 6d / G15 waste-swap mutate BEFORE compilePlacements (solver.js:908) or re-compile after, so walls[] and placements[] can never disagree; (3) make any dropped appliance a validation ERROR ('wallOven requested but not placed') instead of silence; (4) close every run — if a gap >= 1.5" remains after packing, emit an F-filler sized to it, and never place a cabinet/panel past wall.length.

Stop emitting SKUs the catalog can't resolve exactly: snap generated widths to the catalog's width ladder (pair cabinets + filler instead of B3D41), replace pseudo-tokens (EDGTL|..., 'RH21 3624', LR-SQ-8', DWP/FDP/GRILLE) with real catalog codes, and add a solver-output eval asserting every placement resolves with _resolution:'exact' in the active tenant — 'normalized' pricing of solver output is how a $2,463 phantom line appears.

Add the two missing design capabilities the Mautz diff exposes: window-over-sink handling (accept walls[].openings type:'window', suppress uppers there, offer an open shelf) and fridge-anchoring tall pantry (fridge mid-wall, U/T pantry at the run terminal) — plus corner-treatment selection driven by remaining wall budget (choose BBC blind when the adjacent run needs the inches), which also fixes the solver erroring on its own range placement.

Retire nkbaScore=100-with-errors and the 8-boolean scoreAgainstTraining as quality signals; if a layout carries any error-severity validation finding, cap its scores, and report the validator's own errors in the si corpus results so the 180/180 floor can actually fail.

scorer.summary: The 180/180 corpus gate is a validity check, not a quality check: I reproduced a corpus kitchen (K001, single-wall 120") that the scorer passes at 94/100 while containing ZERO base cabinets and ZERO drawers — just fridge/sink/range separated by 3" fillers, a lone 9" upper, and a $1,202 total — because the design metric's only layout signal is an aggregate fill ratio that counts appliances (even the fridge) as "base run", the sink base is typed 'appliance' and thus never counted or priced as a cabinet, and NKBA reports 100 despite 3" sink landings. Severity-'error' validations whose rule name doesn't contain "NKBA" (e.g. K003's 'Cyncly-Range-Fridge-Buffer' — range placed hard against the fridge) are invisible to all five metrics. scoreAesthetics does reach the gate but is toothless: its three sub-scores default to 80/80/70 (composite 76.5, pass ≥60) precisely when there is nothing to evaluate, its `corners` parameter is dead code, and it never looks at uppers-vs-base seam alignment, width regularity, flanking symmetry, talls, islands, or the hood. Nothing anywhere judges a rendered drawing — run-vision.mjs uses vision only to EXTRACT inputs, never to grade outputs. Below is the spec for a scorer that fails today's output the way the owner does: 8 deterministic metrics with formulas on solver output, plus a render→VLM judge built on the existing SSR→resvg pipeline and run-vision.mjs plumbing.

findings.title: A kitchen with ZERO base cabinets and ZERO drawers passes at 94/100
findings.detail: Corpus K001 (single 120", the very first kitchen in the gate) solves to: OVF3 filler, fridge, filler, SB36 (typed 'appliance'), filler, range, filler — no base cabinet carcase at all, no drawer anywhere, one 9" upper + one 36" upper, priced total $1,202. scoreDesign passes because fill=0.85 counts the fridge (TALL zone) and sink toward 'base-run fill' (scoreKitchen.mjs:27 isBaseZone includes appliances) and its ONLY other checks are NaN and cabinet-count>0 (the 2 uppers satisfy it). scorePrice sees only 2 'cabinets' (the uppers) because SB36 is type 'appliance', so the sink carcase is never even priced. This is the owner's 'never been right' in one fixture.
findings.evidence: Live run: `runOne(K001,'eclipse')` → {pass:true, overall:94, design:{score:100, cabinetCount:2, fill:0.85}, price:{total:1202, cabinets:2}}; placements type histogram shows base:0, drawer-SKUs:0. /home/user/End-to-End/evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs:20-27,44-62.

findings.title: Severity-'error' validations bypass all five metrics unless the rule name contains 'NKBA'
findings.detail: K003 (L 120×96) places the range at position 36 directly against the fridge at 0-36 and the solver itself flags severity:'error' rule:'Cyncly-Range-Fridge-Buffer' — but scoreNkba filters validation to /NKBA/i rules (scoreKitchen.mjs:120) and scoreFloorplan reads only result.spatialValidation (line 99), so this hard error gates nothing and K003 passes. Any future solver-emitted error with a non-NKBA rule name is likewise invisible. The floorplan metric also excludes work_triangle_* errors entirely and otherwise trusts the solver's OWN spatialValidation — the scorer grades the solver with the solver's homework (precedent: the mounting-rails silent skip in Phase 0 looked green for the same reason).
findings.evidence: Live run K003: validation errors=['Cyncly-Range-Fridge-Buffer'], run passes. scoreKitchen.mjs:99 (`!/^work_triangle/`), :120 (`/NKBA/i.test(v.rule)`), :96 (sv = result.spatialValidation).

findings.title: NKBA metric reports 100 for a sink whose landings are 3-inch fillers
findings.detail: K001's sink at 42-78 has the fridge to its left (3" filler between) and the range to its right (3" filler between) — NKBA requires 24"/18" sink landings — yet result.metadata.nkbaScore = 100 and the metric passes. Whatever validateNKBA measures for landings, it does not detect the absence of counter-bearing cabinetry beside the sink in this configuration, and the scorer trusts it blindly (scoreNkba reads rep.score, recomputes nothing). Also the pass bar is score≥70 under weights where landingAreas is only 20% (nkba-validation.js:721-733) — a kitchen could zero the landing category and still pass on electrical/triangle points.
findings.evidence: Live run K001: nkba:{score:100, pass:true} with sink flanked by fridge and range at 3" gaps. /home/user/End-to-End/eclipse-engine/src/nkba-validation.js:721-733; scoreKitchen.mjs:116-124.

findings.title: scoreAesthetics auto-passes exactly when there is nothing to evaluate
findings.detail: Its signal does reach the corpus gate (scoreKitchen calls it directly, threshold 60), but: symmetry defaults to 80 when zero balance checks fire (solver.js:8433) — which is the K001 case, since balance only looks at BASE cabinets around interior focal points and K001 has none; consistency awards 80 to walls with no base cabinets (8442); proportionality defaults to 70 (8491). Default composite = 80·0.4+70·0.35+80·0.25 = 76.5 ≥ 60 → a kitchen the scorer literally could not evaluate passes the aesthetics gate. Worst achievable tiers (15/25/25 → 21) require near-universal badness to fail. The `corners` parameter is dead code (never referenced in the body), and talls, islands, the hood, and ALL upper cabinets are excluded from the symmetry/balance model — upper composition is the single most visible thing in an elevation.
findings.evidence: /home/user/End-to-End/eclipse-engine/src/solver.js:8380-8506 (corners unused; :8433, :8442, :8491 defaults); live K001 aesthetic breakdown {symmetry:80, consistency:80, proportionality:55} = two defaults, pass at 71.

findings.title: Consistency sub-metric rewards monotony and penalizes realistic storage mix
findings.detail: solver.js:8449: ≤2 SKU-prefix families on a wall = 100 points. A wall of all door-only 'B' bases (zero drawers — an amateur tell) scores perfect consistency, while a professional mix (B3D drawer bank + SB sink + BWDMA waste + B door base = 4 families) scores 50. The metric is anti-correlated with what a designer calls right. No metric anywhere measures storage-mix realism: drawer-base fraction, presence of a drawer stack near the range, waste pull-out near the sink.
findings.evidence: solver.js:8444-8453; K001/K021 drawer-SKU count = 0 with consistency 80 (default).

findings.title: No metric sees width regularity, flanking symmetry, or upper-base seam alignment — the things a drawing reveals
findings.detail: K001's upper run is a lone 9" W948R next to a 40" gap then a 36" upper — visually absurd, unflagged. Proportionality is a single aggregate ratio (Σ upper width / Σ base-zone width, solver.js:8482) with no distribution term: uppers shoved to one end, a 24" blank over-counter span (K003 wall A, 9"→33"), or uppers whose vertical seams land mid-door on the bases all score identically to a perfectly composed elevation. Nothing checks: hood/upper centered over range, mirror-width flanking around focal points, widths on the 3" module, singleton odd widths (9" next to 42"), or filler budget (K001 spends 12" of a 120" wall on four OVF3 fillers — invisible because fillers are excluded from CABINET_TYPES and from fill).
findings.evidence: Live K001 uppers: W948R pos=5 w=9, W3639 pos=45, gap 14-45; K003 uppers wall A: W948R 0-9, hood 33-75, 24" blank. scoreKitchen.mjs:20 excludes fillers; solver.js:8456-8491 aggregate-only.

findings.title: Price metric has no realism band and skips non-'cabinet' line items
findings.detail: Pass = every CABINET-typed SKU resolves and total > $0. K001 passes at $1,202 for a 10-foot kitchen because only the two uppers count — sink base (typed 'appliance'), fillers, end panels, fridge panels, and the hood are all outside isCabinet, so their resolution/pricing is never checked, and there is no $-per-linear-foot sanity band. A quote missing half its line items or off by 10x passes as long as the surviving cabinets resolve.
findings.evidence: scoreKitchen.mjs:69-90; live K001 price:{cabinets:2, total:1202, pass:true} for a 120" run with fridge+sink+range.

findings.title: No rendered-output judging exists anywhere — 'vision' is input-only
findings.detail: evals/si/run-vision.mjs uses Claude vision solely to EXTRACT rooms from floor-plan images and then scores with the same blind 5 metrics; sample-vision-results.json is an extraction cache. Nothing renders the solver's output (elevation/floor plan SVG) and grades it. Yet the repo already proves the full headless pipeline: SSR-bundle ElevationView/FloorPlanView with esbuild → resvg rasterize (CLAUDE.md render-verify workflow) and has retry/cache/replay plumbing in run-vision.mjs ready to reuse. Gestalt qualities — professional massing, blank-wall awkwardness, composition, 'would a dealer sign this drawing' — genuinely need a VLM judge and are currently unmeasured.
findings.evidence: /home/user/End-to-End/evals/si/run-vision.mjs:1-30 (extraction only, scores via scoreKitchen); CLAUDE.md 'Render-verify without a browser'.

findings.title: The corpus itself cannot exercise the failure modes dealers hit
findings.detail: corpus.mjs generates walls with NO windows, doors, or openings (sink-under-window, clearance-at-door never tested), never uses wall ovens (the OVEN const at line 14 is defined and never referenced by any kit), never sets featureHood or any pref beyond ceilingHeight/sophistication, has no peninsula despite the header comment claiming one, only two ceiling heights, and scales appliance kits DOWN to always fit — so the tight-room compromise paths (solver.js:3286, :3344 'reduced landing' warnings) are structurally unreachable. 180/180 is measured on the easiest slice of the input space.
findings.evidence: /home/user/End-to-End/evals/si/corpus.mjs:14 (OVEN unused), :30-43 (kits), :17-22 (no openings field on any wall), header comment line 6 vs FOOTPRINTS keys.

findings.title: Design metric's fill check tolerates dead gaps and over-fill
findings.detail: fill is a wall-total aggregate: 0.75-1.05 passes. A contiguous 20"+ unusable void mid-run (no cabinet, no filler) passes if the rest compensates; K003 wall B leaves 0-36 empty next to the corner. Over-fill up to 105% (cabinets overrunning the wall by 5%) is explicitly allowed (scoreKitchen.mjs:62). No per-gap or contiguity check exists.
findings.evidence: scoreKitchen.mjs:59-62; live K003 wall B first placement at pos=36.

findings.title: Corner credit is granted for any corner with a sku, unexamined
findings.detail: scoreDesign adds the full two-leg span (up to 72") to baseLen whenever c.sku is truthy (scoreKitchen.mjs:53-58) without checking the corner unit resolves, fits, or that its door swing doesn't collide with the adjacent dishwasher/appliance — corner door-swing conflicts are a classic dealer rejection and are unmeasured.
findings.evidence: scoreKitchen.mjs:53-58; no swing/adjacency logic anywhere in the scorer.

findings.title: Sink base typed 'appliance' corrupts three metrics at once
findings.detail: SB36/SB36-FHD appear in placements with type 'appliance', not 'base'. Consequences: excluded from price resolution (carcase never priced by the metric), excluded from design cabinetCount, excluded from scoreAesthetics balance (baseCabs filter c.type==='base'), and its zone counts toward 'base fill' as if it were an appliance. Whether this is a solver typing bug or a scorer assumption bug, the scorer should count sink/vanity-sink bases as cabinets.
findings.evidence: Live K001 placements: 'appliance SB36'; scoreKitchen.mjs:20-21 CABINET_TYPES has no path for it; price metric shows cabinets:2 on a kitchen with a sink base.

recommendations: SPEC — scoreKitchen v2, deterministic tier (all formulas on solver placements; each would FAIL today's K001/K003 output). M1 Storage-mix realism: baseCabinets = placements where type==='base' OR /^(SB|VSB)/.test(sku); require count >= max(2, floor(totalWallRun/60)); drawerFrac = Σwidth(/B\dD|B2TD/) / Σwidth(base) must be in [0.20, 0.70]; require >=1 drawer bank whose edge is within 36" of the range/cooktop. K001 fails (0 bases, 0 drawers).

M2 Independent landing/counter recompute (stop trusting nkbaReport): walk each wall's placements in position order; counter-bearing = base cabinets + sink + DW; for sink require contiguous counter >=24" one side and >=18" other; range >=15/12; fridge handle side >=15"; require one contiguous prep segment >=30" between sink and cooking surface. Fillers and tall/fridge break contiguity. K001 fails (sink landings = 3" fillers).

M3 Hard-error passthrough: ANY result.validation entry with severity==='error' fails the run, regardless of rule name; keep the NKBA-score check separately. K003 fails today on 'Cyncly-Range-Fridge-Buffer'. Also raise scoreFloorplan beyond self-report: recompute AABB overlap + wall-overrun from placements (position+width <= wall.length + 0.25) independently of spatialValidation.

M4 Composition & width regularity: (a) hood/microwave centerline within 1.5" of range centerline; (b) flanking balance INCLUDING UPPERS: min(L,R)/max(L,R) of upper widths within 36" each side of the hood >= 0.6; (c) no singleton narrow unit: any door/drawer cabinet <12" wide scores an issue unless it abuts a corner or tall; (d) filler budget: Σ filler width per wall <= 6" excluding corner-pull fillers; (e) width-module: fraction of cabinet widths on the 3" module >= 0.8 (per-tenant configurable for metric lines). K001 fails (9" W948R singleton, 12" filler spend).

M5 Upper-base seam alignment + coverage: alignment = fraction of upper vertical seams within 1" of a base seam or appliance edge, require >= 0.5; coverage: no blank upper span > 24" above a counter run unless explained by a window opening, hood, or fridge/tall below. K003 wall A fails (24" blank, 9" upper orphan).

M6 Zone adjacency: range-to-fridge buffer >= 15" of counter (M3 catches today's error, keep as metric so it can't be renamed away); DW edge within 36" of sink edge and on the same run (no corner between); tall units only at run ends (no tall splitting the sink-range counter); waste pull-out (BWDMA) within 36" of sink WHEN present.

M7 Price realism: resolve EVERY placement carrying a sku (sink bases, fillers, panels, hood, accessories) — unresolved non-cabinet items are issues; add per-tenant $/linear-foot band in tenant config (schema field, per MULTI-TENANT RULES — e.g. eclipse: [150, 900] $/lf of base run) and fail outside it. K001's $1,202 for 10 lf fails.

M8 Aesthetic-engine fixes (eclipse-engine/src/solver.js scoreAesthetics): defaults must be 'not applicable' (excluded from composite), never 80/70 free points; include uppers and talls in balance; delete or use the dead `corners` param; invert the consistency incentive to score storage-mix (M1) instead of family-count monotony. Keep threshold but composite only over metrics that actually fired; if fewer than 2 fired, defer to the vision judge.

VISION JUDGE (needed for gestalt — buildable now): new evals/si/run-render-judge.mjs. Pipeline: solve → SSR-bundle ElevationView + FloorPlanView with esbuild (existing render-verify recipe in CLAUDE.md) → resvg PNG per wall + plan → one Claude vision call per kitchen with a rubric returning structured JSON: {composition 1-10, regularity 1-10, storage_realism 1-10, drawing_defects[], would_a_dealer_sign: bool}; pass = all >=7 and no defects. Reuse run-vision.mjs's retry/cache/--json/--replay plumbing verbatim. Seed adversarial goldens: freeze K001's current elevation PNG as a fixture the judge MUST fail (guards the judge itself against drift).

CORPUS v2 (evals/si/corpus.mjs): add wall openings (window over sink candidate, doorways at run ends), wire the unused OVEN into kits for larger footprints, add peninsula footprints (header already promises them), exercise featureHood/sophistication/adaCompliant prefs, and add deliberately TIGHT variants that force the solver's reduced-landing compromise paths (solver.js:3286/:3344) so those warnings are gated, not unreachable.

Rollout: land M1-M8 behind `--v2` in run-corpus.mjs, publish the failure histogram (aggregate() already supports it), fix the solver until v2 is green, THEN promote v2 to the locked floor. Expect the initial v2 run to fail a large share of the 180 — that is the point; today's 180/180 should be treated as the crash/NaN floor only. Also fix the sink-base typing ('appliance' vs 'base') in the solver or normalize it in the scorer first, since three metrics key off it.

cyncly.summary: Cyncly's "auto-design" is real but narrower than the hype: "Inspire Image-to-Design" (aka "AI Inspire to Design" / "Inspire Image to Auto-Design") lives in Spaces Flex, the consumer/retail SaaS launched Dec 2024 — NOT in the professional 2020 Design Live/Design Flex tool. Its pipeline is: user supplies room shape + measurements (manually or via the LiDAR "Cyncly Scan" app, iPhone Pro/iPad Pro only) and picks a layout archetype (galley/L/island) → uploads an inspiration photo → Cyncly-built object-detection models identify products, styles and colors in the photo → matches them to real SKUs in the retailer's loaded catalogs (Content in Cloud) → auto-populates an editable 3D design of THAT room in THAT style, with live catalog pricing. The layout engine underneath is the pre-AI, rule/template-based "Auto-Design Module" lineage from 2020 Ideal Spaces (Home Depot Canada, EUROSTYLE) — the AI layer is image understanding + catalog matching, not a generative layout solver. Headline claim: a 45-minute proposal now takes "a few minutes." The pro tool's "AI" is mostly rendering (auto-lit "Cycles" engine — i.e., Blender's path tracer) plus a 2026 Leads module that pipes consumer Inspire results into Design Flex for a human designer to finish. No independent designer reviews of Inspire's output quality exist yet; trade press is rewritten PR. No evidence of an AiHouse/Coohom engine deal — the CV work appears in-house (job posts cite TensorFlow, image classification, diffusion models). Concretely, "Cyncly did it" = image→style/product matching + template auto-fill + LiDAR scan + huge live catalogs + retail funnel integration. Eclipse's constraint solver already does the one thing Cyncly's consumer flow does NOT clearly do: solve a cabinet layout from walls+appliances without a user-chosen archetype.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: Inspire Image-to-Design is a Spaces Flex (consumer/retail) feature, not a pro-designer auto-designer
findings.detail: Spaces Flex is a SaaS web app launched Dec 2024/Jan 2025 for retailers (online self-service + in-store selling + designer collaboration). Inspire Image-to-Design was announced Feb–Mar 2025 as part of it, marketed as 'transform customer inspiration into fully realized 3D kitchen designs in one click' and 'arguably the biggest advance since 3D CAD.' It won the Esprit Meuble M Award (Services) in Nov 2025 and was shown as a 'first look' with Winner Flex at area30 (Sept 2025) for the German market. The professional tools (2020 Design Live → Design Flex, launched NAM Mar 2025) do NOT ship an auto-layout AI; Design Flex 2026 adds a Leads module that converts a consumer's AI Inspire result into a Design Flex project for a human designer to refine. That handoff is the whole intended workflow: AI produces a lead-gen-grade proposal; a designer finishes it.
findings.applicability: The 'Cyncly did it' myth conflates a consumer lead-gen restyler with professional auto-design. Eclipse's solve() is already positioned where Cyncly is NOT: order-grade automated layout in the dealer tool. The consumer funnel (EmbedApp.jsx + consumer-design.js) is the surface that actually competes with Spaces Flex.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: the exact input→output pipeline (two steps, layout archetype is user-chosen)
findings.detail: Per Cyncly's own Feb 2025 blog and launch PR: Step 1 — consumer/designer inputs the room's layout type (galley, L-shape, island, etc.) and measurements, either manually or via Cyncly Scan, an AI-assisted LiDAR measuring app (iPhone Pro / iPad Pro only) that auto-removes furniture/fixtures/cabinets from the scan and produces a 3D shell + importable floor plan. Step 2 — consumer uploads an inspiration photo; 'AI object detection modules Cyncly developed' identify kitchen products, styles and colors and 'match those to real products that manufacturers offer' by browsing the retailer's catalogs; the system then designs 'a new room that matches the consumer's available space and preferred layout,' output as an editable 3D design with automated quoting from live catalog/pricing data. Marketing phrase used at area30: 'turns lifestyle photos into editable kitchen layouts.' Claimed speed: proposal from 45 minutes down to a few minutes; CEO framing: photo upload or room scan → 'generate thousands of design options' with live pricing, to shrink a 6–9 month purchase journey to weeks.
findings.applicability: Their scan input (LiDAR shell, furniture removal) maps to your FLOORPLAN IMPORT (FP-1/2/3) — you already have vector + vision import; a phone-scan path is the visible gap. Their 'preferred layout' prerequisite means the user constrains the topology; your solver derives placement from walls+appliances+prefs directly.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: the layout engine is template/rule auto-fill with deep pre-AI lineage — the 'AI' is image understanding + catalog matching
findings.detail: The auto-layout machinery predates the AI branding: 2020 Ideal Spaces (the consumer web planner used by Home Depot Canada via EUROSTYLE, Hspace, Principal Kitchens) shipped a literal 'Auto-Design Module' years before Cyncly AI existed, with 'look → completed design in under 20 minutes.' Spaces Flex capabilities pages describe '3D Auto Design': 'after consumers choose from their preferred style and room layout, salespeople can explore initial ideas with them using 3D Auto Design.' Sibling product Winner Flex advertises rule-based automation (auto-complete the room after two walls, automatic worktops/upstands/plinths). So Inspire = (new) photo → object detection → style/product/color extraction → (existing) catalog-constrained auto-population of a chosen layout archetype. Cyncly's own positioning confirms the design step is constraint/catalog-driven, not generative: they explicitly attack Midjourney/DALL-E as 'pixel dreaming' that 'doesn't understand physical constraints,' and claim their differentiator is output that is 'realistic and ready to build' because every element is a real catalog SKU.
findings.applicability: This is the core intelligence for the team: Cyncly did NOT build a generative layout solver — they bolted computer vision onto a 15-year-old template auto-fill engine plus the industry's biggest catalog. Your moat claim ('explainable three-option auto-design' in Finish-Plan-Cyncly-Moat.md) attacks the piece they actually lack. The piece THEY have that you lack is the image→style/product matcher; with your existing Claude-vision plumbing (floorplan.js) an 'inspiration photo → tenant door style/finish/hardware mapping → prefs into solve()' feature is a bounded build, since your tenant catalogs are already structured.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: pro-tool 'AI' is mostly rendering marketing; catalog is the real asset
findings.detail: Design Flex's advertised AI is the 'AI-powered Cycles Rendering Engine' — auto lighting, reflections, materials 'without manual scene setup.' Cycles is Blender's open-source path tracer; the 'AI' component is plausibly denoising/auto-light-placement (inference, but the engine name is theirs). Cyncly Websites offers a consumer photo-restyle visualization tool (upload photo, pick style — diffusion-style imagery for lead capture, not buildable design). Everything quotable runs through 'Content in Cloud,' Cyncly's live manufacturer catalog database ('10,000+ companies' via the Compusoft/Winner heritage) with live pricing — repeatedly cited as what makes their AI output 'shoppable.' Their stated AI strategy: 'trained on the richest catalogue data in the industry,' embedded across workflows.
findings.applicability: Your C3-formula pricing verified to the penny (Mautz 35/35) and per-tenant catalog packages are the same 'real products, real prices' moat at smaller scale. The multi-tenant onboarding pipeline (ingest-spec-book) is your answer to Content in Cloud — breadth of onboarded lines is the race.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: almost zero independent quality evidence exists; observed limits
findings.detail: Extensive searching found no designer forum threads, Reddit reviews, or independent YouTube tests of Inspire Image-to-Design output quality — only Cyncly's own demo videos (e.g. 'Spaces Flex - AI Image to Design', YouTube, Jan 2025) and trade articles that are rewritten press releases (KBBFocus, kbbreview, Wood&Panel, logisticsit). Documented limits: (1) room scan requires iPhone Pro/iPad Pro LiDAR; (2) product matching is bounded by which manufacturer catalogs the retailer has loaded; (3) the user must supply layout type + dimensions first; (4) output is explicitly a starting proposal — Cyncly's Leads module and their own CEO messaging ('human element remains crucial', Kitchens International: 'AI won't replace designers') route it to a human designer; (5) reviews of the underlying pro platform (Capterra/G2, 4.4/5 from a handful of reviews) complain about crashes on v14.2 cloud content, difficulty getting realistic renders, and weak support for non-kitchen spaces — nobody in user reviews praises an auto-design capability. The '45 minutes → few minutes' figure is Cyncly's own, unverified by any third party.
findings.applicability: The competitive bar is lower than the press suggests: nobody has publicly validated Inspire's design quality. Your deterministic eval corpus (180/180 SI sweep, 5-metric scorer, live-vision corpus of 95 real plans) is exactly the proof apparatus Cyncly hasn't shown — publishable side-by-side quality evidence would be a differentiator.

findings.title: TECHNICAL HINTS: in-house CV team, no AiHouse/Coohom engine found, old auto-layout patents exist
findings.detail: Cyncly states the object-detection modules were 'Cyncly developed.' A Sr AI/ML Engineer posting (TA Associates job board) asks for TensorFlow, Python, NLP, image classification models, diffusion models, voice assistants/chatbots — consistent with in-house vision + a diffusion-based visualizer + future assistant features. No evidence of an AiHouse (3vjia) or Coohom/Kujiale partnership or acquisition was found in any press; recent Cyncly M&A is flooring-side (Broadlume, Mobile Marketing, Pacific Solutions). AiHouse/Coohom are competing platforms with their own AI auto-layout, not Cyncly's engine (inference from absence — a private OEM deal can't be fully ruled out). Prior art: USPTO patents exist for automatic kitchen-cabinet layout generation optimizing 'functionality, visual appearance, price' (e.g. US11270034, assignee unverified) and 20-20's own US6801218 (auto-relocating utility openings) — rule-based auto-layout is old, patented ground; Cyncly's Cyncly-AI-branded push (2024–2026, under CEO Anand Krishnan, appointed Apr 2024) is a productization wave, not a research breakthrough.
findings.applicability: No hidden super-engine to fear. The realistic threat model: Cyncly's distribution (installed base + catalogs + retail funnel) delivering 'good-enough' template auto-fill with a slick photo-matching front end. Beat it on solver quality (real placement logic, NKBA validation, explainability), quote verifiability, and tenant onboarding speed — and close the two visible gaps: inspiration-photo style extraction and phone LiDAR room capture.

sota.summary: Survey of automated layout generation for a kitchen-cabinet auto-design engine. Generic learned scene-synthesis models (ATISS, SceneFormer, DiffuScene, LayoutGPT) dominate the academic literature but output continuous positions/sizes for free-standing furniture, need thousands-to-hundreds-of-thousands of training scenes, and are a poor fit for a domain where every box must be a real catalog SKU and NKBA rules are hard constraints. Classical discrete optimization (0-1 MILP/CP, constrained search) fits the cabinet-run domain almost perfectly — kitchen layout has literally been formulated as 0-1 integer programming — but its quality ceiling is the quality of the objective function. Commercial "AI auto-furnish" tools (Coohom/Kujiale, Planner5D, Homestyler) run learned models over enormous proprietary designer-layout corpora and produce inspiration-grade general furnishing, not SKU-exact priceable cabinetry; IKEA Kreativ is CV scene capture + manual drag-drop, not auto-layout; a USPTO kitchen-cabinet patent (US11270034) reveals industry uses generate-candidates-plus-cost-function (symmetry, price, unused space). The strongest architecture for this domain is the hybrid: (1) beam/best-first search over discrete per-wall SKU compositions scored by the existing 5-metric rubric (deterministic, zero training data, hard constraints native, incremental from the current packer); (2) a CP-SAT/MILP layer for exact global decisions (corner treatment, appliance-wall assignment, filler minimization) doubling as a diverse top-K candidate generator; (3) LLM-as-planner over the solver's input DSL (Holodeck/LayoutGPT pattern) for high-level design-intent variation and as an offline judge to tune scorer weights — kept out of the deterministic hot path. Training a generative scene model is explicitly de-recommended.

findings.title: (a) Classical: kitchen layout has been directly formulated as 0-1 integer programming / CP
findings.detail: A 2024 Charles University thesis ('Kitchen Layout Generation as an Optimization Problem', Kološ) models kitchen cabinet/fixture/appliance placement as a 0-1 MILP and a MiniZinc CP model — discrete slots, catalog-like unit widths, adjacency and appliance rules as hard constraints, an objective over workflow/coverage. Related: 'Generative Layout Modeling using Constraint Graphs' (Para et al., ICCV 2021) generates layouts by predicting a constraint graph then solving a constrained optimization; 'Automatic Generation of Constrained Furniture Layouts' (arXiv 1711.10939) similarly separates constraint specification from solving. Properties: fully deterministic (fixed solver + tie-breaking), zero training data, optimal within the encoded objective, moderate engineering cost (OR-Tools CP-SAT is free and fast at this scale — a kitchen is tens of discrete decisions, not thousands). Quality ceiling: bounded by the objective — a MILP with a naive objective reproduces exactly the 'valid but mediocre' failure mode; the design taste has to live in the objective/scoring, not the solver.
findings.applicability: Direct fit. The engine's domain (per-wall 1D sequences of catalog widths + a handful of global couplings: sink wall, dishwasher adjacency, corner treatment, cooking-zone centering, work triangle) is a textbook discrete assignment problem. A CP-SAT model can replace the greedy pass ordering with exact joint optimization of the decisions the heuristic passes (normalizeSinkPlacement, centerCookingZone, fitIslandToRoom) currently make sequentially and irrevocably. NKBA rules from constraints.js become hard constraints; the SKU catalog is the domain of each variable, so 'every box is a real SKU' is satisfied by construction.

findings.title: (a) Classical: simulated-annealing/MCMC cost-function optimization (Make It Home lineage)
findings.detail: Yu et al., SIGGRAPH 2011 ('Make it Home') optimizes a hand-built ergonomic cost function (visibility, accessibility, pairwise relationships extracted from exemplars) via simulated annealing with Metropolis-Hastings moves; a perceptual study found results indistinguishable in functionality from human designers. This is the canonical 'design quality = cost function quality' result: the search method is generic, all the intelligence is in the scoring terms and exemplar-derived priors. Weaknesses for this domain: stochastic (deterministic only with fixed seed and even then fragile across code changes), designed for continuous 2D placement of free-standing furniture rather than discrete abutting runs, and slower than exact methods on small discrete spaces.
findings.applicability: The lesson to steal is not annealing itself (the discrete cabinet-run space is small enough for exact/beam search) but the cost-function design: encode pairwise and ergonomic priors (landing areas each side of range/sink, symmetry about focal points, drawer-stack distribution, filler penalties) as explicit scored terms — which is exactly what the repo's evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs 5-metric scorer already started. TRAINING_PROFILES in solver.js is a primitive version of Make It Home's exemplar-derived priors.

findings.title: (a) Classical: shape grammars / procedural rules — the incumbent approach, known ceiling
findings.detail: Procedural/rule-tree systems ('Automatic Interior Design in AR Based on Hierarchical Tree of Procedural Rules', MDPI 2021) and the ML-assisted procedural pipeline of 'Linear kitchen layout design via machine learning' (AI EDAM 2022 — six chained classifiers, random forest best, trained on a designer-built linear-kitchen dataset, integrated into Unity) show the pattern: deterministic, cheap, low data, but quality equals rule quality and degrades on rooms outside the rule authors' anticipation. The AI EDAM paper is the closest published work to cabinet-run design specifically and its scope (linear kitchens only) illustrates the generalization ceiling of pure rules/classifier pipelines.
findings.applicability: This is essentially what the current greedy packer + heuristic passes already is. The literature says the escape from its ceiling is not more rules but wrapping rule-based generation in search + scoring (see hybrid finding). The AI EDAM classifier-pipeline route (predict next unit given context) is not recommended: it needs a labeled kitchen dataset the team doesn't have and still can't jointly optimize.

findings.title: (b) Learned scene synthesis (ATISS, SceneFormer, DiffuScene, COFS): high ceiling for open scenes, poor fit here
findings.detail: ATISS (NeurIPS 2021) treats a room as an unordered set of objects and autoregressively samples category/position/orientation/size with a transformer; SceneFormer conditions autoregressive transformers on floor plan/text; DiffuScene (CVPR 2024) denoises an unordered set of object-attribute vectors (location, size, orientation, semantics, shape feature) and beats prior SOTA on plausibility/diversity on 3D-FRONT; COFS adds controllability. Quality ceiling: high for naturalistic free-furniture rooms — they learn real designer distributions. Costs: (1) data — trained on thousands of professionally designed 3D-FRONT rooms; an industrial cousin ('Deep Layout of Custom-size Furniture', arXiv 2012.08131, from the Kujiale/Coohom ecosystem) used 710,700 professional designs — dealer teams have nothing comparable for kitchens; (2) outputs are continuous positions and sizes, so every emitted 'cabinet' must be snapped to a legal SKU width and repaired against NKBA rules, and abutting-run geometry (boxes must tile a wall exactly, corners consume two legs) is precisely what set-of-boxes models are worst at; (3) sampling is stochastic — determinism requires seed-pinning and even then retraining changes everything; (4) engineering cost is highest of all options (training infra, dataset curation, eval drift).
findings.applicability: De-recommended as the core engine. The cabinet domain's hard constraints (exact tiling, real SKUs, code rules) would force so much post-hoc projection/repair that the learned prior's value is mostly destroyed. The one transferable idea: learn or fit the *scoring* distribution (what designers prefer) rather than the *generator* — see hybrid finding.

findings.title: (b) LLM approaches: LayoutGPT (in-context numeric layout) and Holodeck/ReSpace (LLM proposes, solver disposes)
findings.detail: LayoutGPT (NeurIPS 2023) is training-free: retrieval of in-context exemplars + a CSS-like structured DSL lets GPT-4-class models emit numeric 3D scene layouts 'comparable to supervised SOTA (ATISS)' on bedroom/living-room benchmarks — but it still hallucinates collisions/out-of-bounds placements at a nontrivial rate. Holodeck (CVPR 2024) is the more robust pattern: the LLM emits *relational constraints* from a fixed 10-type vocabulary (edge/middle, near/far, in-front-of, aligned, face-to), and a deterministic DFS solver with collision checking produces the actual placement, with error reports fed back for iterative repair. ReSpace (2025) adds preference alignment (training the generator against human/scored preferences); arXiv 2506.07570 does multi-stage preference optimization on synthetic human-aligned data. Properties: near-zero training data (in-context), high semantic quality ('understands' style/adjacency intent), but per-call cost/latency, nondeterministic unless temperature-0 + pinned model, and numeric outputs untrustworthy without a validator.
findings.applicability: The Holodeck division of labor maps 1:1 onto this codebase: the LLM should never emit cabinet positions or SKUs — it should emit the solver's own input language (prefs, zone assignments, feature choices, 'which wall gets the sink/hood', design-option variants), and the deterministic engine realizes it into real SKUs. This also matches the roadmap's 'three-option explainable auto-design': LLM proposes three distinct design intents, engine solves each, scorer ranks. Keep the LLM out of the deterministic hot path (optional/cached/offline) so evals stay reproducible; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plumbing for this already exists via the floorplan vision function.

findings.title: (c) Commercial systems: learned auto-furnish at consumer grade; kitchen cabinetry remains template/manual; capture ≠ layout
findings.detail: Coohom (international arm of Kujiale) advertises chat/AI-driven design and auto-placement of branded products into 3D scenes; the Kujiale ecosystem's published research (custom-size furniture layout trained on 710,700 professional designs) indicates deep-learned placement over a massive proprietary corpus — an unreplicable data moat, and its public output quality is 'good general furnishing suggestion', not order-grade cabinetry. Planner5D's AI furniture placement and Homestyler AI similarly analyze room geometry and suggest several editable arrangements from real-catalog items — explicitly positioned as suggestions the user then adjusts. IKEA Kreativ (built on acquired Geomagical Labs) is primarily spatial capture: CV/stereo scans produce an editable 3D replica, users erase and drag-drop IKEA items; its kitchen planning remains a separate, largely manual configurator. The clearest industry signal for the cabinet domain is patent US11270034 ('Method and system for kitchen cabinet layout'): generate candidate cabinet layouts and select via a cost function with explicit terms for cabinet symmetry, price, and unused space — i.e., industry practice for real cabinetry is generate-then-score with hand-designed terms, not end-to-end learning. 2020/Cyncly and Winner, the incumbent dealer tools, are template-assisted manual design, which is precisely the gap the roadmap's 'explainable auto-design' targets.
findings.applicability: Two takeaways: (1) no commercial system demonstrably auto-generates SKU-exact, code-compliant, priceable cabinet runs — a working scored-search engine is genuinely differentiating vs Cyncly; (2) don't chase the Coohom architecture — it's built on a designer-corpus scale the team cannot reach, and its output grade wouldn't survive the order-readiness gate anyway.

findings.title: (d) RECOMMENDED #1: beam/best-first search over discrete per-wall SKU compositions + rubric scoring (generate-candidates-then-score)
findings.detail: The pattern with the best fit: enumerate legal SKU sequences per wall via beam search (each beam state = partial run; expansions = catalog SKUs legal at that position given constraints.js), keep top-k partial compositions by an admissible partial score, couple walls through the small set of global variables, and rank complete kitchens with a full-design scorer. Precedent: production sequence generation universally uses beam + second-stage reranker; 'A Novel Framework for Automated Warehouse Layout Generation' (arXiv 2407.08633) applies exactly constrained-beam-search-plus-scoring to industrial layout; the US11270034 patent is the same shape (candidates + cost terms); Make It Home supplies the cost-term vocabulary. Properties: deterministic (fixed beam width, stable tie-breaking), zero training data to start, hard constraints native (illegal SKUs are simply never expanded — 'every box is a real SKU' by construction, NKBA violations pruned at expansion), quality ceiling raised continuously by improving the scorer rather than rewriting generation, engineering cost low-moderate and fully incremental: the current greedy packer is the beam=1 special case, and evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs (design/price/floorplan/NKBA/aesthetic) is already the reranker — it just isn't in the solve loop yet. Runtime is controllable (beam width × wall length / 3-inch grid keeps candidate counts in the thousands, well within interactive budgets for a pure-Node solver).
findings.applicability: Concretely: refactor solver.js's per-wall packer into generate-k-candidates; move the heuristic passes' decisions (sink placement, cooking-zone centering, corner treatment, tall/fridge wall) into enumerated branch points; score complete candidates with a solve-time port of the si scorer plus price and filler terms; return the argmax (and expose top-3 as the roadmap's three explainable options — each candidate's score breakdown IS the explanation). Evals (397/0, 180/180) remain meaningful because the whole loop stays deterministic.

findings.title: (d) RECOMMENDED #2: CP-SAT/MILP layer for exact global structure, doubling as a diverse candidate generator
findings.detail: Where beam search is myopic (global couplings like work-triangle geometry across walls, corner units consuming two legs, minimizing total filler across the whole room, symmetric flanking of the range), a small integer program is exact and still deterministic. The Kološ thesis proves the whole kitchen fits in 0-1 IP; Para et al. (ICCV 2021) shows constraint-graph + optimization scales to furniture layouts. Modern CP-SAT solves this size in milliseconds and can enumerate the top-K optimal-and-diverse solutions (solution pools / diversity constraints), which feeds recommendation #1's scorer with structurally different candidates rather than beam-local variations. Cost: a real modeling effort (2-4 weeks to encode constraints.js faithfully) and a native/WASM solver dependency in an otherwise pure-Node engine — OR-Tools has Node bindings, or run it as a build/serverless step. Quality ceiling: optimal for whatever the objective encodes; pair with the rubric scorer so 'optimal' tracks design quality, not just packing efficiency.
findings.applicability: Best used surgically: keep the JS engine as the realizer, and use CP-SAT for the global skeleton (appliance-to-wall assignment, corner strategy, tall placement, run budgets per wall) whose solutions parameterize the per-wall beam search. This directly attacks the greedy engine's real weakness — early irrevocable decisions — without rewriting the parts that already work (SKU realization, elevations, pricing).

findings.title: (d) RECOMMENDED #3: LLM-as-planner over the solver DSL + LLM/vision-as-judge for scorer tuning (Holodeck pattern, kept off the hot path)
findings.detail: Two bounded LLM roles with strong precedent: (1) Planner — as in Holodeck (LLM emits relational constraints, deterministic solver places) and LayoutGPT (in-context DSL emission), have the LLM translate customer intent ('lots of baking storage, hide the fridge, modern minimal') into the engine's existing input schema (prefs, featureHood, zone weights, design-option branch choices) and into 2-3 named design intents; the deterministic engine + scorer does everything else, so hallucination cannot produce an illegal SKU or NKBA violation. (2) Judge — as in ReSpace/preference-aligned layout work (arXiv 2506.02459, 2506.07570), use an LLM/vision judge offline over rendered elevations/floorplans (the SSR→resvg pipeline makes this headless-able) to grade candidate pairs, and fit the rubric scorer's weights to those preferences — buying learned design taste with hundreds of judgments instead of hundreds of thousands of training scenes. Determinism: preserved, because both roles run offline or as optional pre-processing; the core solve stays pure. Data needs: near zero (in-context + a modest judged set). Cost: prompt engineering + the existing serverless key plumbing.
findings.applicability: Fits the existing 'live-vision corpus of 95 real plans' and self-improving-QA direction: the judge closes the loop that turns the si scorer from hand-tuned to preference-calibrated, which is what raises the quality ceiling of recommendations #1/#2 over time. The planner role slots into the consumer funnel (EmbedApp) where free-text intent arrives, and into the three-option explainable auto-design phase of the Cyncly moat plan.

findings.title: Cross-cutting comparison table (quality ceiling / determinism / data / cost / SKU-NKBA fit)
findings.detail: MILP-CP: ceiling = objective quality; deterministic yes; data none; cost moderate; SKU/NKBA fit native (constraints by construction). Simulated annealing: ceiling = cost-function quality; deterministic only if seeded; data none; cost low; fit good but overkill vs exact methods on this discrete space. Shape grammar/procedural (status quo): ceiling = rule quality (known-mediocre); deterministic yes; data none; cost sunk; fit native. ATISS/SceneFormer/DiffuScene: ceiling high on open furniture scenes but degraded by SKU-snapping; deterministic no; data 10^3-10^5 designed scenes; cost highest; fit poor (continuous outputs vs exact tiling + catalog). LayoutGPT: ceiling comparable-to-supervised on generic rooms, unproven on cabinetry; deterministic no; data none; cost low; fit poor if emitting geometry, good if emitting DSL. Holodeck-style LLM+solver: ceiling = solver+scorer quality with semantic intent on top; deterministic in the solver half; data none; cost low-moderate; fit excellent when the LLM is restricted to the DSL. Beam-search + rubric/learned rerank: ceiling = scorer quality and rises with it; deterministic yes; data optional (judge-tuned weights); cost low-moderate, incremental; fit native. Commercial learned auto-furnish (Coohom-class): ceiling consumer-inspiration grade; data 10^5-10^6 proprietary designs; unreachable and unnecessary for order-grade cabinetry.
findings.applicability: Final recommendation ordering for this engine: ship #1 (beam + solve-time scorer) first — it is the smallest delta with the largest quality gain and preserves every eval floor; add #2 (CP-SAT global skeleton) when beam-local myopia shows up in the si corpus; layer #3 (LLM planner + judge-calibrated scorer weights) to lift the ceiling from 'valid and good' to 'looks designed', without ever putting a stochastic model between input and SKU output.

method.summary: Ground truth for a "right" kitchen assembled from three layers: (1) the NKBA Kitchen Planning Guidelines, which supply hard numeric minimums (42"/48" work aisles, 26-ft triangle with 4–9 ft legs, per-appliance landing areas, DW within 36" of the sink, seating knee-space by counter height, 158" total frontage); (2) uncodified compositional craft from working designers and cabinet-industry guides — five-zone planning (consumables/non-consumables storage, clean, prep, cook), a hood-centered symmetric range wall, the 3"-increment width grid with fillers ≤3" as a last resort, uppers aligned to bases, talls consolidated at run ends, drawer-base preference in modern work, and island sizing/overhang rules; (3) a consistent professional decision sequence: appliances + sink/venting locked FIRST, then tall anchors at run ends, then zones assigned to the remaining counter runs, then base fill on the width grid, then upper composition around focal points, then a filler/sliver cleanup pass. Delivered as a 10-step ordered decision process and a 28-item machine-checkable rubric (13 hard NKBA gates pass/fail + 15 soft craft items, overall pass = all hard + ≥80% soft) that maps directly onto the eclipse-engine solver's existing passes (normalizeSinkPlacement, centerCookingZone, featureRangeWall, scoreAgainstTraining) and the evals/si 5-metric scorer.

findings.title: NKBA hard numbers — circulation and the work triangle
findings.detail: Work aisle (counter edge to opposing counter/island/wall where work occurs): >=42" for one cook, >=48" for multiple cooks. Walkways where no work occurs: >=36". Work triangle (sink, primary cooking surface, refrigerator, measured center-front to center-front): sum of three legs <=26 ft, each leg >=4 ft and <=9 ft; no island/peninsula may intersect a leg by more than 12"; no full-height obstruction (tall pantry, fridge column) may stand between two work centers; major household traffic should not cross the triangle. Sources: Wholesale Cabinet Supply NKBA explainer, Mod Cabinetry NKBA guideline list, CRD Design Build, NKBA Planning Guidelines with Access Standards PDF (newcreationsaustin.com mirror).
findings.applicability: Directly checkable from solver output: placements[] gives center-front of SB/range/fridge; walls[] + island give aisle widths. Add as hard gates in evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs NKBA metric; fitIslandToRoom should enforce the 42/48 aisle, and the triangle test should treat talls[] as obstructions.

findings.title: NKBA hard numbers — landing areas per appliance
findings.detail: Sink: >=24" of counter on one side and >=18" on the other. Cooking surface: >=12" on one side and >=15" on the other; on an island/peninsula additionally >=9" of counter behind the cooktop; never place a cooktop under an operable window; vertical clearance above cooktop 24" to a protected/noncombustible surface (hood) or 30" to unprotected/combustible (cabinet). Refrigerator: >=15" landing on the handle side, or within 48" of the front (also 15" adjacent to undercounter refrigeration). Microwave and oven: >=15" landing above/below/adjacent (oven landing may be across an aisle <=48" away if traffic permits). Prep area: >=36" wide x 24" deep continuous counter immediately adjacent to a sink. Total countertop frontage: >=158" at 24" deep with >=15" clearance above. Sources: Wholesale Cabinet Supply, Mod Cabinetry, isd-kitchencabinet NKBA list, Simply Cabinetry.
findings.applicability: The solver already emits per-wall cabinet sequences with widths; landing checks are run-length sums between an appliance SKU and the next tall/wall/corner. These become 6-7 discrete rubric gates; several (range 12/15, fridge 15) are cheap to enforce inside the per-wall 1D packer as placement constraints rather than post-hoc scoring.

findings.title: NKBA hard numbers — dishwasher, corners, seating
findings.detail: Dishwasher: nearest edge within 36" of the nearest edge of a cleanup/prep sink; >=21" of standing space between the DW edge and any counter/appliance/cabinet placed at a right angle (this effectively bans DW jammed into a corner). Seating clearances: 24" of width per seated diner; knee space depth by counter height — 18" deep at 30" high, 15" at 36" high, 12" at 42" high; behind seating allow 36" (no traffic passes) to 44" (walkway behind diner). Corner treatment: corner storage should be functional (lazy susan, blind unit with pull-out hardware) — a sealed dead corner is a recognized defect; also keep appliance/cabinet doors at inside corners from clashing. Sources: Mod Cabinetry, isd-kitchencabinet.com, NKBA Planning Guidelines PDF, ShelfGenie and Nelson K&B corner-solution guides.
findings.applicability: DW-within-36 and DW-21-standing are one-line checks on placements[]. Corner functionality maps to the existing BBC/BL/BLS family handling; the si scorer's corner-span fix (Phase 0) already credits two-leg span — add the inverse check that a corner intersection has SOME corner unit or intentional dead-corner filler, never an unreachable void. Island seating checks read prefs.island + overhang.

findings.title: Zone-based planning — the craft layer NKBA doesn't codify
findings.detail: Working designers plan in five zones, an evolution of the triangle: (1) consumables storage (fridge + pantry together), (2) non-consumables storage (dishes/cutlery, near DW), (3) cleaning (sink+DW+trash), (4) prep (the largest continuous counter, ideally between sink and range), (5) cooking (range/oven + pots/pans/utensils within arm's reach). Placement grammar: pantry adjacent to fridge; prep zone touches both clean and cook zones; dish storage within one step of the DW; trash pull-out in the clean zone near the prep edge; workflow reads storage -> prep -> cook, with clean positioned so dirty dishes flow sink-ward without crossing the cook. Each zone needs its own counter frontage AND its own storage — a zone with counter but no cabinets (or vice versa) is a miss. Sources: Houzz 'New Ways to Plan Your Kitchen's Work Zones', Hunts Kitchen Designs zones guide, Cabinet IQ, Kitchen Solvers, Verity Jayne zone-planning blog.
findings.applicability: The solver's TRAINING_PROFILES scoring is the natural home: score zone adjacency (pantry|fridge adjacency, prep-between-sink-and-range, DW-adjacent dish storage as drawer bases near sink) rather than only global aesthetics. This is metric #1 candidates for the si 'design' score.

findings.title: Range wall composition — hood centered, symmetric flanks, one focal point
findings.detail: Consensus designer rules: the range wall is the focal wall; the hood is the focal object and must be centered over the range, and the range centered on its wall segment (or on an architectural axis) whenever possible. Cabinets flanking the hood should be mirror-symmetric in width — upper symmetry matters more than base symmetry because the eye reads the wall, not the toe space. Hood/hood-surround slightly wider than the range (e.g. 36" range, 42-48" hood chase) reads intentional. Tall cabinets used as flankers need real visual weight — skinny talls beside a hood look accidental. Avoid competing focal points: one wall carries the composition, others support. Where perfect symmetry is impossible, designers use 'balanced asymmetry' — equal visual mass, not equal widths — but a program should target true symmetry first. Sources: Tami Faulkner Design range-wall elevations article, CliqStudios 'Symmetry & Balance' and '7 Kitchen Design Principles', Houzz symmetry discussions, Decor Cabinets balanced-asymmetry piece.
findings.applicability: centerCookingZone and featureRangeWall already exist — extend to (a) assert |left flank width - right flank width| <= 3" for uppers beside the hood, (b) center the range on the wall segment net of talls, tolerance +/-3". This is a checkable symmetry score: reflect the upper sequence about the range centerline and diff widths.

findings.title: Width rhythm — the 3" grid, sliver avoidance, fillers as last resort
findings.detail: Stock/semicustom cabinets come in 3" increments, 9"-48" (9,12,15,...,48). Craft rules: prefer door cabinets 15-24" per door (no door wider than ~24" — matches the existing doorCount rule), drawer bases 18-36" (drawers below ~15" lose too much interior to the box), avoid any cabinet under 12" unless it is a dedicated pull-out (tray/spice/filler-pull-out); a 9" sliver door cabinet is a recognized amateur tell. Fillers: normal in small amounts for scribe and door-swing (1.5-3"), but keep total filler per run <=3" and never place a filler mid-run — fillers go against walls and into corners; a filler wider than 3" means the size mix should be re-chosen (bump one cabinet up/down a size). Repeating widths creates rhythm: runs read best when widths repeat or step monotonically toward the focal point rather than random sequences like 33-12-27-15. Sources: Kitchen Cabinet Kings filler guide, Inspired Kitchen Design 'fillers and panels' mistakes article, D&G Flooring cabinet-width guides, Foreverbuilt 3-inch increment guide.
findings.applicability: The 1D packer's width-selection heuristic should optimize: minimize filler total (<=3"/run), forbid <12" boxes except designated pull-out SKUs, prefer symmetric/repeating width multisets. Rubric items: max single filler 3", total filler per run 3", zero sub-12" non-pullout cabinets, door-width cap 24" (already in ElevationView's doorCount — move the rule upstream into the solver so drawings and solve agree).

findings.title: Vertical composition — uppers match bases, common datum, tall consolidation
findings.detail: Elevation craft: (a) upper cabinet vertical joints should align with base joints where possible, or follow a deliberate pattern (e.g., uppers symmetric about the window even if bases aren't); upper run ends should land flush over base run ends, not overhang. (b) One top datum: all uppers and talls share a crown/top line (top-anchored, as the engine already does with upperTopAFF); over-fridge and over-range cabinets are depth/height exceptions on the same datum. (c) Talls consolidate: pantries and oven towers belong at the ENDS of runs or grouped into a single storage wall with the fridge (fridge+pantry tall block); a tall mid-run that chops the countertop in two is a canonical layout error; tall placement must also not break a landing area or stand between two triangle work centers. Making the tall 2" deeper than bases so the counter edge dies into its side reads deliberate. Sources: 10 Percent Cabinetry tall-pantry planning guide, Houzz '10 Clever Ways to Finish a Cabinet Run', WOODWEB base/upper alignment threads, Coohom kitchen-elevation guides, gardenweb/Houzz symmetry threads.
findings.applicability: Checkable: for each wall, tall positions must be at index 0 or last (or adjacent to fridge); count counter-run fragments per wall (>2 fragments on one wall = fail). Upper/base joint alignment = compare cumulative-width breakpoints of uppers[] vs walls[] bases within +/-1.5", scored as fraction aligned. The engine's top-anchored uppers already satisfy the datum rule — assert it stays true.

findings.title: Modern storage preference — drawers over doors at base level
findings.detail: Contemporary practice (especially frameless/European lines like Eclipse and pronorm) strongly prefers drawer bases to door bases for everything except the sink base, corner units, and talls: drawers bring contents to the user, doors force crouching. Designer guides recommend the majority of base storage as drawer stacks (3-drawer 24-36" units) in the prep and cook zones — pots/pans in deep drawers flanking or under the range, utensils in top drawers at the prep zone. Door bases survive where drawers can't: sink base, corner, sub-12" pull-outs. A reasonable modern target: >=50-60% of non-sink/non-corner base frontage as drawer bases; a traditional/framed brand target can sit lower (~40%). Interiors of deep pantries should be roll-outs/drawers to stay usable at 24" depth. Sources: 10 Percent Cabinetry planning guide, Block Renovation cabinet-planning guide, Fabuwood/CliqStudios design-principles articles, Houzz zone articles.
findings.applicability: Rubric item computed from SKU families: fraction of base run width in B3D/B4D/B2TD vs plain B door bases, excluding SB/BBC/BL. Make the threshold a tenant capability field (per the multi-tenant rule: a config number like prefs/tenant 'drawerBaseTargetPct', never if(brand)).

findings.title: Island composition rules
findings.detail: Minimum useful island: ~24" deep counter for work, >=30-36" deep if seating (overhang needs support of depth); seating overhang 12" (42" bar height) to 15-18" (30-36" heights); 24" of edge width per stool; clearance around the island 42-48" on working sides (36" absolute floor on pure walkway sides); an island longer than ~10 ft without a break/level change starts to read as a barrier and impede circulation; if the island carries the sink or cooktop, all landing rules travel with the appliance (incl. 9" behind an island cooktop) and the DW stays within 36" of the island sink. Composition: the island's working side faces the range wall; seating faces the working core from the outside; island cabinet joints should echo the perimeter rhythm; waterfall/panel ends finish exposed sides. Sources: Angi island-size guide, by-crea overhang and seating guides, D&G Flooring island dimensions, Laurysen Kitchens island-mistakes article, Fabuwood island size guide.
findings.applicability: fitIslandToRoom already sizes to aisles; add gates for seat count x 24", overhang depth by height, landing rules when normalizeSinkPlacement puts the sink on the island, and the 10-ft break heuristic. Seating knee-space depths (18/15/12) come from the NKBA finding above.

findings.title: How professionals SEQUENCE decisions — the ordered process
findings.detail: Consistent across Harvey Jones (UK bespoke), Block Renovation, Best Online Cabinets' designer-process writeup, and NKBA-trained designers: (0) capture room facts — walls, windows/doors, ceiling, plumbing/gas/vent stubs; (1) LOCK APPLIANCES + SINK FIRST (exact models/sizes), with venting and plumbing, before any cabinet is drawn — 'design the cabinetry first and fit appliances into gaps' is the named amateur mistake; sink usually keeps the window/plumbing wall, range goes to the ventable focal wall, fridge lands at the perimeter of the work core nearest the entry; (2) verify triangle + aisles at appliance level (cheap to fix now); (3) place TALL ANCHORS at run ends — fridge surround + pantry as one tall block, oven tower at a run end — which fixes where continuous counter runs begin and end; (4) assign ZONES to the remaining runs (clean at sink, prep on the largest run between sink and range, cook around range, dish storage at DW); (5) fill bases zone-by-zone on the 3" grid, DW beside sink, corners resolved with dedicated corner units, drawer stacks in prep/cook; (6) compose UPPERS as elevation work — symmetry about hood and window, joints aligned to bases, one top datum; (7) add the island last, sized to surviving aisles; (8) cleanup pass — redistribute widths to kill fillers >3" and slivers <12"; (9) score against guidelines and iterate. Sources: Harvey Jones '5 Decisions', Block Renovation kitchen-cabinet planning ('three things get locked before any cabinet is drawn: appliances, venting, buy order'), Best Online Cabinets 'Kitchen Design Process', Homes & Gardens 'How to Design a Kitchen', Tami Faulkner 'Optimizing a Kitchen Design'.
findings.applicability: This is nearly the pass order solver.js already uses (normalizeSinkPlacement -> centerCookingZone -> pack -> fitIslandToRoom) — the missing explicit stages are (3) tall-anchor placement BEFORE base packing and (8) a width-redistribution cleanup pass; adding them as named passes would let the si scorer attribute failures to a stage.

findings.title: THE RUBRIC — 28 machine-checkable items with pass thresholds
findings.detail: HARD GATES (NKBA-derived, any failure = not order-grade): H1 min work aisle >=42" (>=48" if prefs.cooks>1). H2 walkways >=36". H3 triangle sum <=26ft. H4 each leg 4-9ft. H5 no tall/full-height obstruction between two work centers; island intersects a leg <=12". H6 sink landing 24"/18". H7 range landing 15"/12"; +9" behind island cooktop. H8 fridge landing >=15" handle side (or <=48" across). H9 DW edge <=36" from sink edge. H10 DW has >=21" standing clearance (not corner-jammed). H11 continuous prep counter >=36"x24" adjacent to a sink. H12 cooktop not under operable window; hood clearance 24"/30". H13 seating: 24"/seat, knee depth 18/15/12 by height 30/36/42, >=36" behind seats (44" with traffic). SOFT CRAFT (score 0-1 each; pass overall = ALL hard + >=80% soft = >=12/15): S1 five zones each have both counter frontage and storage. S2 pantry tall adjacent (or <=48") to fridge. S3 prep zone lies between sink and range on the workflow path. S4 dish storage (drawer base/upper) within 36" of DW. S5 range centered on its wall segment +/-3" (net of talls). S6 hood centered over range, hood >= range width. S7 upper flanks of range mirror-symmetric within 3". S8 sink centered under window +/-2" when a window exists. S9 upper joints align to base joints (>=60% of joints within 1.5") or follow a declared symmetric pattern. S10 single top datum for uppers/talls (over-fridge exception). S11 talls only at run ends or grouped; no wall's counter broken into >2 fragments. S12 no cabinet <12" wide except designated pull-out SKUs; no door >24". S13 filler discipline: max single filler 3", total per run <=3", none mid-run. S14 drawer-base fraction of eligible base frontage >= tenant target (default 50%). S15 island: work side faces range wall, overhang per height, joints echo perimeter rhythm, length <=10ft unbroken. SCORING: report hard failures as blockers (maps to orderReadiness.js order-grade gate), soft as a 0-100 craft score; suggested weights equal, but S5-S7 (focal wall) and S13 (fillers) doubled if a single aesthetic number is wanted — these four are the strongest human 'looks designed vs generated' signals per the designer sources.
findings.applicability: Every item is computable from the solver's existing emitted geometry (placements[], walls[]/uppers[]/talls[], island, _elev, _inputWalls windows/doors) with no new data. Natural implementation home: extend evals/si/scoreKitchen.mjs — H1-H13 fold into the NKBA metric, S1-S15 split across design (S1-S4), aesthetic (S5-S11, S15), and a new width-rhythm submetric (S12-S14). Thresholds that are taste-dependent (S7 tolerance, S14 target) should be tenant/prefs config fields per the multi-tenant rule.

claim.title: Greedy per-wall solve with no global objective, no backtracking
claim.detail: solve() solves each wall independently (solveWall loop) after a fixed heuristic wall-assignment (longest wall = range+fridge, second = sink). The work triangle, aisle clearances, and cross-wall balance are only VALIDATED afterward — never optimized. When placement fails, 'rescue' passes re-pack appliances evenly instead of reconsidering earlier choices. A trivially ordinary input (L-shape 160"/130", 5 appliances) triggers the error path: range initially placed at 0 with a 'Wall A is too short' error on a 160-inch wall, then a work triangle of 368" (legs 135"/184" vs 108" max) that the solver merely warns about.
claim.evidence: solver.js:644-655 (per-wall loop), 480-517 (heuristic assignment), 2971-3305 (sequential per-appliance scoring, no joint search), 3307-3352 (rescue re-pack), live run output: 'Tight-Landing-Reduced-Clearance ... placed at 0' + 'work_triangle_large 368" > 312"' on walls 160/130

verdict.evidence: Ran solve() on the exact claimed input (L-shape 160"/130", range 30/fridge 36/sink 33/DW 24/hood 30, no pins, no prefs). Reproduced everything: (1) output.validation contains severity=error 'Tight-Landing-Reduced-Clearance: Wall A is too short to give the range (30") its full NKBA landing area — it was placed at 0"' on the 160" wall that holds only 66" of appliances; (2) the message is also stale/false — centerCookingZone (solver.js:8130, called at :703) later moved the range to position 42, but the 'placed at 0' error ships anyway; (3) work triangle legs Sink→Range 134" and Fridge→Sink 183" (both > 108" NKBA leg max), total 365" > 312" max (claim said 368"/135"/184" — identical within rounding), emitted by spatial-validator.js:600 validateWorkTriangle as severity 'error' then explicitly DOWNGRADED to advisory 'warning' by the ADVISORY_RULES set at solver.js:1876-1885, so the violating layout ships; (4) also unoptimized in the same run: walkway 36"<42", sink secondary landing 0"<18". Architecture claims verified against source: solveWall is invoked exactly once per wall (solver.js:652, the only call site) with no feedback from any validation; heuristic wall assignment at 480-517 (longest wall → range+fridge, second → sink); sequential one-appliance-at-a-time scoring loop at 2971-3305 with no joint search; rescue pass at 3307-3352 evenly re-packs primaries on the SAME wall (gap=(span−totalBody)/(n+1)) and never reconsiders wall assignment or earlier placements. Mechanism of the bogus 'too short' error fully diagnosed: corner reserve 36" + fridge reservation 36" leave an 88" range zone; the scorer requires BOTH flanking gaps to be in _VALID_GAPS (sums of stock widths 9-42, all multiples of 3, solver.js:2796-2813); the gaps sum to 58" — not divisible by 3 — so snapToNearestValid returns null for every candidate, bestPos stays null, and the body-fit fallback (3259-3288) fires the false error; ranges have no relaxed second pass (sinks do, line 3068), and no backtracking on the fridge/corner reservation exists.
verdict.rootCause: eclipse-engine/src/solver.js — greedy single-pass architecture: fixed heuristic wall assignment (lines 480-517) places range+fridge on the longest wall and sink on the second with no work-triangle objective; positionAppliances (2852-3385) places appliances sequentially and its _VALID_GAPS snap constraint (2796-2813, 3390-3402) rejects every position whenever the free span is not a sum of stock widths (here 58", not a multiple of 3), triggering the false 'wall too short' body-fit fallback (3259-3288); work-triangle/aisle/landing checks run only post-hoc (spatial-validator.js:600, nkba-validation.js) and solver.js:1876-1885 downgrades their errors to advisory warnings; solveWall has exactly one call site (652) — no backtracking or re-solve path exists, and the rescue pass (3307-3352) only re-packs the same wall.

claim.title: Width selection is largest-first greedy; composition is never an objective
claim.detail: fillSegment/greedyFill packs stock widths largest-first (42 then 36...), then patches the remainder with fillers or width-mods (regex SKU rewrite). This produces runs like B42-RT + B16-RTL flanking a range (42" vs 16") and a B3D10 (10-inch three-drawer base) — widths no designer would draw. Because widths freeze here, every later symmetry pass can only permute boxes, never resize them, so the 42/16 flank is unfixable downstream. The repo's own comments call an off-center range 'a classic auto-generated tell'.
claim.evidence: constraints.js:1627-1679 (greedyFill largest-first), solver.js:3487-3599 (fill + mod patching); live run: wall A = B42-RT | range | B16-RTL, wall B ends in B3D10

verdict.evidence: Reproduced verbatim by running solve() (eclipse-engine/src/index.js). (2) Exact claimed B3D10: L=112/121/124/139/142/154/172 with fridge+sink+range+DW → B3D10 minted by greedy 9" base + width-mod 9→10; also B3D9/B3D11/B3D13/B3D14. (3) Sweep L=100-260 x 3 appliance kits (483 runs): 21 walls with >=2x nearest-base flank asymmetry, 363 non-stock-width bases, 39 bases <=10". (4) On the shipping 180/180 si corpus itself: 23 twelve-inch bases in rangeFlanking/sinkAdjacent zones and 17 width-mods including B3D48 (42→48), B4D48, BWDMA48, BWDMA23 — and findSku() confirms B3D10/B3D9/B3D48/B4D48/BWDMA48/BWDMA23/B16-RTL/B10L are all absent from the pricing catalog (phantom SKUs on quotable output). (5) Code confirms the architecture: greedyFill (constraints.js:1667-1679) is pure largest-first; fillSegment returns immediately on exact greedy fill (line 1633) so composition is never scored, and each side of the range is a separate independently-filled segment (no cross-flank objective); the symmetric branch fires only on inexact fills with preferSymmetry. fillWallSegment (solver.js:3487-3599) patches remainders with fillers or regex SKU rewrite (sku.replace(/\d+.*$/,'')). centerCookingZone (solver.js:8130-8192) — whose own comment at solver.js:698-699 calls an off-center range "a classic 'auto-generated' tell" — only permutes boxes (width-conservation guard at line 8180), so frozen widths make the 42/16 flank unfixable downstream, exactly as claimed. Bonus defects observed: SKU/width mismatches (B42-RT at 41.25", B22 1/16-RTL at 15.75") and range appliance widened to 47.25".

claim.title: Symmetry/centering passes can only reorder, not redesign — and silently no-op
claim.detail: centerCookingZone and centerSinkUnderWindow search prefix-splits of existing movable cabinets around anchors; they conserve widths and revert on any anomaly (both wrapped in try/catch non-fatal). In the reproduced run the best achievable prefix split left the range flanked 42/16 (centering 'succeeded' per the decision log while flanks stayed 2.6:1). applyRangeFlankSymmetry only fires when BOTH neighbors are plain bases. Symmetric width selection would have to happen during fill, where symmetry is only a boolean hint (preferSymmetric) on one zone type.

Final wall A: B42-RT[42@0] range[36@42] B16-RTL[16@78] refrigerator[36@94] — flanks 42/16 = 2.63:1, range center 60" vs span midpoint 47" (still 13" off-center) — while result.decisions contains: 'Range re-centered at 60" on wall A with balanced flanking cabinets — an off-center cooktop reads as an accident.' Both neighbors are plain bases, so 29/29 was trivially achievable by resizing, but centerCookingZone only permutes (width conservation asserted at solver.js:8180) and applyRangeFlankSymmetry never re-runs after it. (2) WORSE CASE: galley 198"/168" with fridge@0, range@123: final flanks are a 3" filler (OVF3) vs a 42" base (14:1 immediate ratio; run flanks 83.25/48) with the same 'balanced flanking cabinets' decision logged. (4) Code mechanics confirmed at cited lines: centerCookingZone (8130-8192) and centerSinkUnderWindow (8038-8122) search only prefix splits of existing cabinets, conserve total width, and swallow all errors per-wall (8120, 8190) plus the outer try/catch at 702-709; the 'balanced flanking cabinets' decision at line 706 fires unconditionally on any commit regardless of achieved balance; applyRangeFlankSymmetry (2730-2771) bails unless BOTH immediate neighbors are plain bases (2740) and each flank ≥15" (2756), and runs only at solveWall time (2711) — before centering — so it can neither repair nor veto centering's reorders; the only width-time symmetry input is preferSymmetric at solver.js:3488, passed solely for zone==='rangeFlanking', and constraints.js:1636-1647 only uses it to mirror one segment's internal split when greedy fill leaves a filler — it never coordinates the two flanks around the appliance. claim.title: No room geometry model inside the solver
claim.detail: Corners are inferred from wall ARRAY ORDER (walls[0]/walls[1] assumed adjacent, all 90 degrees unless an explicit turn field), not from wall endpoints. The work-triangle coordinate builder maps every wall after index 0 onto the same y-axis at x = wallA.length — so triangle math is fiction for U/G shapes (wall 3 of a U gets wall-B coordinates). The Drawing-Quality-Audit confirms galley wall B draws outside the room because both walls share one frame; per CLAUDE.md the actual world-frame logic lives in FloorPlanView, not the engine. Islands are placed by the renderer with defaults (audit A5).
claim.evidence: solver.js:2022-2034 (corner pairs by index), 8319-8331 (2D coords wrong for >2 walls), docs/Drawing-Quality-Audit.md A1/A5, CLAUDE.md ('FloorPlanView ... per-wall world-frame logic that the 3D view reuses')

verdict.evidence: Ran solve() on the shipped u_shape_family template (walls A=156, B=120, C=156). (1) Wall inputs carry no endpoints (only {id,length,role}); resolveCorners (solver.js:2016-2057) pairs corners purely by array index per layoutType, 90-degree assumed unless wallB.turn is exactly 45/135. (2) The 2D coordinate builder (solver.js:8319-8331) maps EVERY wall after index 0 onto x=wallA.length: range on wall C gets (156,78) vs true (78,120); fridge gets (156,138) vs true (18,120). Computed legs: fridge-to-sink 179.0 in vs true 122.4; total 377.1 vs true 307.7 — so solve() emits a FALSE NKBA-Triangle-Max violation ('Work triangle 377 > 312 maximum') on its own flagship U template (true total is compliant), plus wrong leg numbers (138/179 vs true 125/122). (3) Galley repro (two 120-in walls, 48-in aisle): wall B is treated as perpendicular hinged at x=120 — sink-to-range computed 78.7 in (true across-aisle ~49); emitted 'Range-to-fridge 118 > 108 too far' warning where true distance ~64 in. A second validator (linear-stacker.js distance2D: cross-wall distance = a.x + b.x Manhattan-from-wall-start, not from the shared corner) reports yet different numbers (129, 360) — two mutually disagreeing fictions in one solve() output. (4) _spatialModel.walls labels ALL walls of a U-shape "direction":"NORTH" — the so-called spatial model has no headings/endpoints either. (5) solve().island output contains no x/y (only length/depth/workSide/etc), confirming the renderer places islands; docs/Drawing-Quality-Audit.md A5 confirms FloorPlanView/3D re-place the island with their own defaults, and A1 (P1) confirms galley wall B draws outside the room because both walls share one frame. Eval corpus (180/180) never catches this because no eval checks cross-wall distances against real room geometry.
verdict.rootCause: eclipse-engine/src/solver.js — buildLayout's 2D coordinate builder (lines 8316-8331, every wall idx>0 collapsed onto wall B's frame) and resolveCorners (lines 2016-2057, adjacency by array index, no endpoints in the wall input schema); compounded by eclipse-engine/src/linear-stacker.js distance2D (line ~761, cross-wall = a.x+b.x) as a second inconsistent distance model, and by island placement living in frontend/src/FloorPlanView.jsx / Kitchen3DView.jsx instead of the engine. NKBA work-triangle validation in constraints.js (validateLayout, lines 1788-1825) consumes the fictional coords, so U/G/galley kitchens get false violations and masked real ones; per-wall 1D packing itself remains correct, which is why layouts still 'pass' evals.
